articles.title: Jessica Pegula: Tennis Influencers Have Become 'A Little Too Much' at US Open
articles.summary: Pegula said she also can appreciate what influencers can bring to the sport.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Jessica Pegula thinks influencer behavior at the US Open this year is starting to go too far.

The world No. 3 player was asked Wednesday about crowd etiquette at the tournament following multiple viral videos of influencers using lights during matches at Arthur Ashe, and said she feels it's "gotten a little maybe too much" this year.

"People are down there trying to perform, and it's their career and their job," Pegula said after winning her second-round match Wednesday. "And it seems a bit disrespectful."

Pegula, who is known as one of the most active player representatives on the tour , said she understands that influencers can bring attention to the sport

"I think I can appreciate the influencers coming and kind of showcasing the US Open experience," Pegula said "I think that's something that the US Open has utilized a lot as far as food and drinks and things to do and the shops. That part is part of a fan experience and something that people might not know and make them want to go."

But she draws the line when they are disrupting play: "I can appreciate one side of it, but I think we have the other side literally interrupting matches, it gets a little tough."

Pegula's comments come just weeks after she told FOS she believes influencers have helped "grow the sport."

"They've brought a lot of eyes to the sport and made it more trendy. We're seeing tennis as having kind of its crossover Hollywood moment, you're seeing more fashion and celebrities at a lot of these big tournaments," Pegula said earlier this month.

Aryna Sabalenka, the No. 1 ranked women's player, also voiced her support for influencers when asked by FOS last week: "I love it, I love it. It's more eyes on [our] sport."

Former US Open champion Daniil Medvedev said Wednesday he thinks the added attention on tennis thanks to content creators has "more upside than downside."

"In general, the more the sport grows, the better it is," Medvedev said. "So I would say this way: I trust USTA with what they are doing. For sure, if it disturbs during the play, like if you see the light or something … But I'm pretty sure as well, even then, maybe one time they do it, and then someone tells them not to do it."

But some former players are more hesitant, particularly because of rising ticket prices.

"It's maybe not the greatest thing for the real tennis fan because they've started getting priced out of the market," Patrick McEnroe told FOS last week.

Genie Bouchard told FOS last week that she has "two minds" about influencers .

"I obviously want everyone who wants to go to [the US Open] to be able to go, and true fans to be able to watch. So if it's more brands or influencers or taking up these spots, then there's a bit of sadness to that," Bouchard said.

The USTA did not respond to a question about whether it was considering banning spectators from bringing equipment, such as ring lights and flash cameras. However, US Open head of communications Brendan McIntyre told FOS the tournament is reminding attendees to "refrain from any activity that can disrupt the action" in a number of ways, including "in advance of event emails to ticket holders, notifications to suite holders, and messagings on video boards."

"It should be noted that these instances happen infrequently, and similar to when crowd noise reaches a certain level, our chair umpires have the ability to address the crowd when they occur," McIntyre added.

articles.title: El PSG no empieza con buen pie
articles.standfirst: Casino Gran Madrid nos ofrece las cuotas especiales sobre la Ligue 1
articles.summary: Casino Gran Madrid nos ofrece las cuotas especiales sobre la Ligue 1
articles.body: El PSG afronta esta temporada con el objetivo de conquistar su sexto título consecutivo de Ligue 1, algo que le convertiría en un dominador absoluto del fútbol francés en la última década. Sin embargo, el arranque del conjunto de Luis Enrique no ha sido el esperado. Los parisinos suman dos empates en sus dos primeras jornadas, primero ante el Rennes y después frente al Lille, y todavía no conocen la victoria en el campeonato pese a llegar como vigentes campeones de Liga y de la Champions League. Un doble pinchazo que contrasta con la solidez mostrada la pasada campaña, cuando el equipo se paseó prácticamente en solitario por la clasificación. Pese a este inicio irregular, las casas de apuestas no dudan a la hora de señalar al PSG como el gran favorito para levantar el título en mayo. Casino Gran Madrid paga la victoria final del conjunto parisino a una cuota de 1.19, una cifra que deja bien a las claras que el mercado interpreta estos dos empates como un simple bache de inicio de temporada y no como el reflejo de una crisis de mayor calado. La plantilla de Luis Enrique, con el añadido de haber revalidado la Champions League la pasada primavera, sigue siendo la de mayor nivel individual y colectivo de todo el campeonato francés a gran distancia del resto. El segundo favorito para Casino Gran Madrid es el Mónaco, a cuota 11, un dato que también encuentra respaldo en el terreno de juego. El conjunto del Principado ha arrancado la temporada con pleno de victorias, superando al Le Havre y al Olympique de Marsella, y llega a la visita al Parque de los Príncipes este viernes en un estado de forma muy superior al de su rival. Por detrás aparece el propio Marsella, a cuota 16, y ya mucho más alejado el Lille, a 30, pese a haber sido capaz de sacarle un empate al PSG en la última jornada. Más allá de la lucha por el título, el mercado también ofrece alternativas interesantes para quienes buscan otro tipo de valor en sus apuestas deportivas. Para terminar la temporada entre los tres primeros clasificados, Casino Gran Madrid paga al Mónaco a cuota 1.75, consciente de que su gran inicio de temporada le da argumentos de sobra para pelear una plaza europea de forma directa. El Marsella aparece en este mercado a 2.05, mientras que el Lille se sitúa en 2.65, ambos con opciones reales de completar una campaña que les permita clasificarse para competición continental. Por último, y pensando en un mercado que excluye directamente al conjunto parisino de la ecuación, Casino Gran Madrid ofrece la cuota de "victoria sin el PSG", es decir, quién sería el campeón si el equipo de Luis Enrique no formara parte de la clasificación. En este apartado, el Mónaco vuelve a aparecer como principal candidato, a cuota 2.9, por delante del Marsella, a 3.8, y del Lille, a 5.5. Estas cifras confirman que, más allá del nombre propio del PSG, existe un grupo reducido de equipos con argumentos reales para pelear por todo en una Ligue 1 que, temporada tras temporada, sigue mostrando una brecha muy marcada entre el líder y sus perseguidores.

articles.title: Fantasy Football: Hayden Winks' top-five most important lessons learned from Yahoo Fantasy Expert League Draft
articles.summary: These lessons might just help you in your final fantasy football drafts this weekend.
articles.body:
The Yahoo Expert League was a 12-team live draft streamed on YouTube. You can watch our analysis and pick-by-pick reactions for full context, but after taking part in the draft myself, I learned some things that will help you during draft weekend. Here are the top-five lessons learned from this half PPR league, one we will be playing out as a real league.

Everyone in the room expressed nervousness about missing out on RBs. This was evident as high as third overall, when Justin Boone drafted Jonathan Taylor, even though it disagreed with his own and everyone's raw rankings. He knew (and was right) that the RB options at the Round 2/3 turn were going to be ugly, and he didn't want to go Zero RB.

Ditto for Scott Pianowski when he took Kyren Williams at 2.07 over literally any of the WRs in the Round 2 tier. Travis Etienne Jr. went 3.02, and Javonte Williams went 3.05. I've seen those players in the fourth round more often than the third round, but in a room full of full-time fantasy analysts, the RBs went at a premium early on.

Josh Allen went at 3.07. That's even after his Yahoo ADP, but his selection was instantly met with live roasts from all of the veteran drafters. Allen has been 18th and 30th overall in my half-PPR fantasy points over replacement per game metric in four straight seasons, but this was more of a supply-and-demand analysis done by the rest of the league.

Pianowski led the vocal charge of mocking every early-round QB selection, knowing he'd get very startable QBs with his last picks. He did just that by drafting Brock Purdy in Round 11 and Jordan Love in Round 14. He had five WRs, four RBs and his TE before selecting his first QB, and it's hard to argue with the results. Streaming Purdy and Love based on matchups will lead to a top-10 scoring QB this year, and he didn't have to spend up for it.

I didn't press my luck that far, but Jayden Daniels was my QB in Round 8 after drafting his top WR, Terry McLaurin. I can defend a three-round premium from Purdy to Daniels, but the fact that I was also able to grab Bo Nix in Round 13 shows the viability of late-round QB this year. Nix was the QB9 in back-to-back seasons and added Jaylen Waddle this offseason.

Lamar Jackson was the 5.12 for those curious, but Caleb Williams fell to 8.12 and Jalen Hurts was 7.03 if you're looking for what I'd view as the sweet spot of waiting on QBs.

It was hard to justify any of our selections from the 5.10 onward. I selected Terry McLaurin at 5.09, and that was easy to defend. My co-host Josh Norris was upset by that, as he had the following selection. He didn't like anyone, paused and ultimately selected Sam LaPorta way ahead of ADP. Zero-floor dead zone RB Bhayshul Tuten went 5.11 and Lamar Jackson rounded out the round. Both picks were mocked by the room.

Unfortunately, there is just a massive tier break at RB and WR in this range. There's no way around it. Some opted to pick the semi-elite QBs, like Drake Maye (6.03) and Joe Burrow (6.08), but as just outlined, it's hard to defend the two-vs.-twos with the teams who waited on QBs until Round 8+. Others took on massive injury risks, like Tucker Kraft (6.01), Mike Evans (my 6.03), J.K. Dobbins (6.09) and MarShawn Lloyd (6.10 — more on him below). It's hard to defend Evans' continued soft-tissue injuries, but the other WR options were Brian Thomas Jr., Marvin Harrison Jr. and Carnell Tate. Tough.

Round 7 was filled with potential NFL team No. 2 RBs like Jonathon Brooks (7.02), Blake Corum (7.04), Chuba Hubbard (7.09) and Kyle Monangai (7.11). Hubbard has done it before but the others have never been top-20 options. The fact that they are in consideration this highly shows how bad this range is.

Eat your vegetables with a TE or veteran WR here because the more heart-racing upside swings are being drafted in Rounds 8+.

Lloyd went 6.10 to Justin Boone, who was elated by his perceived fall. Some believe Lloyd is a Round 5-6 value, while the consensus is probably closer to Round 7-9.

I took Jacobs with 9.09 as my RB4, fully knowing what the range of outcomes are. If charges are somehow dropped or if the Commissioner's Exempt List ultimately follows the Personal Conduct Policy's outline of six game suspensions for first-time domestic violence acts, then the ninth round will likely be of great value (purely in fantasy football terms of course). I'd say that explains about 50% of the outcomes. The remaining 50% of outcomes include an indefinite placement on the Exempt List while they attempt to learn more about the situation or a full Packers release and permanent ban from the NFL if the alleged video is leaked and shows what is alleged to have happened. It's not fair that this is how it works in the world, but the video leaking or not by Week 6 very well could determine if Jacobs is playing in November and December this year. Most players who are suspended for domestic violence continue to play. The exceptions are the ones with video attached.

Quickly on Lloyd, I'm fading him at these new draft prices. Most importantly, it's probably close to 50% that Jacobs is just back halfway through the season, and that's when it's easiest to find other starters in the RB2 and FLEX spots. Beyond that, Lloyd's very unproven, and his injury history could be so extensive that the coaching staff doesn't want to go from 0 to 20 touches per game. It's possible, if not likely, that he's in a committee with Chris Brooks available for pass protection and Kaleb Johnson or Pierre Strong available for change-of-pace duties. Jacobs was the RB12 as a real bellcow last year, and I'd be very hesitant to project Lloyd for the same volume. He'll be the RB20 or so in my early-season weekly rankings.

This training camp was a long one, with many highly-drafted players leaving with injuries. Here's where they went, and my take on the picks:

Ashton Jeanty at 2.21: Very fair. After Hampton, Achane, Henry, Brown, etc.

Malik Nabers at 3.01: Very fair. I'd draft him even earlier if needed. Around 20th.

Jeremiyah Love at 3.09: Very fair. It was my selection, after all. I was stoked.

Rashee Rice at 3.11: Ehhh. Risky in half-PPR with Ladd McConkey, Tetairoa McMillan, Garrett Wilson available.

Emeka Egbuka at 4.05: Fair. He went at the bottom of a big WR tier. Turf toe is real.

Tucker Kraft at 6.01: Ehhh. There will be a ramp-up period and negative regression.

Jonathon Brooks at 7.02: Ehhh. Experiencing soreness after multiple years missed.

Alec Pierce at 7.07: Ehhh. Practicing but slight limp when walking after big surgery.

Kyle Monangai at 7.11: Bad. Everyone groaned.

George Kittle at 8.10: Fair. He's apparently traveling for Week 1. This is a quick return.

Mike Washington Jr. at 10.5: Ehhh. This is a bit early if Jeanty is playing Week 1 or 2.

Jordyn Tyson at 10.10: Fair. Better click in redraft with IR spots. Week 9 return is likely.

articles.title: Mid-game brawl leads to charges for youth football coaches
articles.summary: The youth sports league has suspended the coaches indefinitely.
articles.body:
Three Pennsylvania youth football coaches were charged Thursday, days after they were part of a massive brawl caught on video during the final minutes of a game, police said.

The clash took place during the final minutes of Saturday's game between Carlynton and Keystone Oaks in Carnegie, a Pittsburgh suburb. An unidentified Carlynton coach was seen screaming at the sideline of the opposing team and then confronted one of their coaches, the video showed.

Although referees tried to separate them, the fight escalated as more Keystone Oaks coaches came onto the field and fought with the Carlynton coach.

At one point during the fight, a Keystone Oaks coach and the Carlynton coach were seen throwing a punch at the other's head as bystanders looked on and called to watch the kids.

On Thursday, the Carnegie Police Department said that the Carlynton coach, who they allege threw punches "which would have caused substantial harm and most definitely caused serious inconvenience," was charged with disorderly conduct and harassment summons.

Police also charged two unidentified Keystone Oaks coaches with disorderly conduct summonses, the police said.

The investigation is ongoing. Attorney information for the coaches wasn't immediately available.

Steel City Youth Football League, which organized the game, said in a statement Monday that it suspended two coaches involved in the fight indefinitely.

The two teams independently suspended five additional members involved in the clash, according to the league.

"League officials are reviewing video footage, referee reports, and witness statements. The scope of this inquiry is not limited to the ejected individuals; the investigation may expand to include additional personnel, coaches, or spectators found to be involved," Steel City Youth Football League said in a statement.

articles.title: Quinnen Williams: Cowboys' Defense 'Night And Day' From Last Season
articles.summary: Cowboys star defensive tackle Quinnen Williams raved about new defensive coordinator Christian Parker's setup: It's like "night and day."
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys have a lot of new faces on defense, including defensive coordinator Christian Parker, and one of the featured elements of their defense is pumped about how they're shaping up on that side of the ball. "The growth, it's like night and day," Cowboys star defensive tackle Quinen Williams said about the team's defensive growth on Wednesday, according to the Cowboys' team website. "Starting in OTAs, and starting the first week of training camp, getting a chance to go against one of the best offenses in battle every single day has helped us tremendously. The mindset coming from the coaches, top down to the players and to the leadership, has been drastically changed. It's just fun, man. "I just can't wait to see the process and the results from all the hard work. But, we're not done yet." In 2025 under defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus, Dallas was last in the NFL in opponent passing yards (251.5 per game) and opponent points (30.1 per game), 30th in opponent total yards (377.0 per game), tied for 22nd in sacks (35.0) and 10th outright in opponent rushing yards (125.5 per game). The year prior (2024), the Cowboys were 31st in opponent points and 28th in opponent total yards under defensive coordinator Mike Zimmer. For context, the Cowboys were fifth in opponent points in 2022 and 2023, seventh in opponent points in 2021 and fifth in opponent total yards in 2023. The aforementioned success came under defensive coordinator Dan Quinn, who left Dallas after a three-year stint in the role (2021-23) to become the head coach of the Washington Commanders. The Cowboys moved on from Eberflus in favor of Parker, the former Philadelphia Eagles passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach. This is Parker's first stint as an NFL defensive coordinator. "It's been amazing — from where we started off in OTAs to where we are at now," Williams said about the team's defensive progression. "We've got some fine-tuning, some things to clean up, some things to do, but I feel comfortable. The progressions that we made, the growth and the development that we have made, and to go into the right direction that we wanted to go into." Dallas signed Williams, a 2022 All-Pro and a Pro Bowler in each of the last four years, to a three-year, $105.9 million extension in August, with the $35.3 million average annual value second among NFL interior defensive linemen. He ranked second among defensive linemen with an 88.8 overall grade and seventh with 51 total pressures, according to Pro Football Focus. As for the players joining Williams, Dallas signed safety Jalen Thompson (three-year, $33 million deal) and cornerback Cobie Durant (one-year, $4 million deal) and acquired veteran linebacker Rashan Gary from the Green Bay Packers, among other moves. Regarding the draft, the Cowboys traded up one spot to select Ohio State Buckeyes safety Caleb Downs with the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft and also selected UCF Knights linebacker Malachi Lawrence with the No. 23 pick. Dallas opens its 2026 regular season on the road against the New York Giants on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Hugh Jackman Wants To Buy Soccer Club To Rival Ryan Reynolds And Wrexham
articles.summary: Hugh Jackman wants to join his fellow Hollywood star and friend Ryan Reynolds in owning part of a soccer club in the English leagues.
articles.body: Hugh Jackman wants to join his fellow Hollywood star and friend Ryan Reynolds in owning part of a soccer club in the English leagues. Jackman has long been a fan of Norwich, his mother’s home city in the east of England. The Wolverine star was asked in an interview broadcast on Thursday if he would like to "buy a bit" of the club which is majority owned by Mark Attanasio, the Milwaukee Brewers principal owner. "I’m very, very interested in talking about it right now," he told British broadcaster TalkSport while promoting his new movie, "The Death of Robin Hood." "You’re the first one to know that. There’s a little exclusive," Jackman said when asked if he would "follow suit" with Reynolds, who put Wrexham on the global soccer and culture map after buying the club with Rob Mac in 2021. Norwich and Wrexham are now rivals in the English second-tier Championship, though Jackman’s team has the more illustrious history. Norwich last played in the Premier League four years ago, and had perhaps its finest moment in 1993, eliminating German power Bayern Munich in the old UEFA Cup. "Good on Ryan, you do your thing, I’m all about the Canaries," Jackman said, citing Norwich’s nickname linked to the team’s distinctive yellow and green uniform. Norwich and Wrexham both are expected to be contenders this season to earn promotion to the Premier League, the world’s most valuable club soccer competition. "I think it’s an exciting team and it’s going to be an exciting year," Jackman said, praising Norwich’s turnaround since hiring Belgian coach Philippe Clement last November. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Lionel Messi To Get Mid-Game Tributes By Soccer Teams Across Argentina
articles.summary: Soccer teams across Argentina will pay tribute to Lionel Messi with a mid-game minute of applause during their next match following his decision to retire from international duty.
articles.body: Soccer teams across Argentina will pay tribute to Lionel Messi with a mid-game minute of applause during their next match following his decision to retire from international duty. Referees will pause play at the 10-minute mark of every match in the upcoming round of the Clausura tournament, as well as in other men's and women's leagues in Argentina, in appreciation of Messi’s career with the national team, the Argentine Football Association said late Wednesday. The 39-year-old Messi, who wore the No. 10 jersey for Argentina, announced on Monday he will no longer play for the national team after 21 years of service. He led Argentina to the World Cup title in 2022 as well as two other World Cup finals, and made 207 appearances and scored 125 goals — both national records. Messi, who is idolized in Argentina, has never played professionally in his home country. He moved to Barcelona at the age of 13 to began a once-in-a-generation career and is regarded by many as the greatest player of all time. Messi is continuing to play at club level with Inter Miami in Major League Soccer. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Mullins pleased to bring competition to Newport squad
articles.summary: Hayden Mullins believes 15 new faces can provide both cover and competition in his Newport County squad.
articles.body:
Hayden Mullins believes Newport County have strength in depth after a frantic end to the transfer window.

Newport have added 15 players this summer, including six loanees, with Michael Adu-Poku, Kion Etete, Tanatswa Nyakuhwa and Matty Jacob all joining on deadline day.

And County boss Mullins is welcoming tough selection decisions.

"It's a good problem to have. It's better to have more bodies with a lot of quality around it than not have [those options]," he said.

"We're going to need the squad. We've got a lot of selection doubles in most positions, which is what we wanted.

"We wanted to create competition in all areas of the pitch and keep people on their toes and I feel we have done that."

Newport have started the season in encouraging goal-scoring form with only Bristol Rovers bettering their nine goals in four games in League Two.

So Mullins is not concerned by a lack of goals among his new signings given Nyakuhwa is yet to score in senior football while Adu-Poku and Etete last netted in 2024.

"Our style of play is one which is generating goals and chances," he said.

"Shaq [Gwengwe] has only been at this level for four games and scored four. Yahya [Bamba] has got a goal and Harrison Biggins, so our lads in the higher areas are generally contributing with goals.

"So hopefully the new guys come in and add to their tallies as well."

"We've identified Michael [Adu-Poku] as a powerful winger with pace, someone who we feel could really help us and fit into our style.

"We know Tan [Nyakuhwa] pretty well. He was here last season and was someone we had to be patient with."

Mullins has also secured Cardiff City forward Etete on loan and is convinced his aerial presence can help end the former Tottenham youth player's wait for a league goal, which stretches back to February 2024.

"Kion wanted to come and we had an opportunity to take a player whose level should be higher than League Two," said Mullins.

"It was a decision we had to make last minute and I'm glad we made it because it bolsters our attack really well."

Etete will not be available immediately, however, after suffering a minor hamstring issue while playing for Cardiff under-21s.

Mullins was also delighted to secure Hull City left-back Matty Jacob on a short-term loan with Tom Davies likely to be out until Christmas with an ankle injury.

While Newport have scored plenty, no other team in League Two has conceded more than the Exiles and Jacob's experience will help, having relied on 18-year-old Alfie Merritt to cover Davies.

The NHL has officially released the Prime Video schedule for the 2026-27 season, giving Canadian hockey fans a look at the 27 games that will be available exclusively on the streaming service as part of Wednesday Night Hockey. The schedule features some of the biggest teams and stars in the league, with the Toronto Maple Leafs, Montreal Canadiens and Edmonton Oilers among the clubs receiving the most exposure.

The schedule begins September 30 with the New York Islanders visiting the Toronto Maple Leafs, a matchup that could feature the first meeting between 2025 No. 1 pick Matthew Schaefer and 2026 No. 1 pick Gavin McKenna.

Maple Leafs, Canadiens and Oilers headline the schedule

The Maple Leafs will appear on Prime Video six times, while the Canadiens lead all Canadian teams with seven appearances. The Edmonton Oilers will appear five times, followed by the Calgary Flames, Winnipeg Jets and Ottawa Senators with four appearances apiece. The Vancouver Canucks are scheduled for two Prime Video games.

There are plenty of notable matchups throughout the schedule.

The Canadiens will visit Alex Ovechkin and the Washington Capitals on October 14, while Brady Tkachuk's return to Ottawa with the Florida Panthers is scheduled for October 21. One week later, the Battle of Alberta between the Oilers and Flames will be featured on Prime Video.

The 27-game schedule is part of a much larger agreement between Prime Video and Rogers. The companies agreed to a 12-year deal that makes Prime Video the exclusive Canadian home of Wednesday Night Hockey through the 2037-38 season.

Prime Video will also exclusively stream two first-round Stanley Cup Playoff series and one second-round series each year in Canada. The regular-season games and playoff series will be available in both English and French to Canadian Prime subscribers at no additional cost.

The opening matchup could be particularly intriguing, with McKenna expected to make Toronto's roster after being selected first overall in the 2026 NHL Draft. Schaefer, meanwhile, was the first overall pick in 2025 and won the Calder Trophy last season.

Prime Video is clearly becoming a major part of the NHL's Canadian broadcasting landscape, and the 2026-27 schedule gives fans plenty of reasons to tune in on Wednesday nights.

articles.title: Fall Sports Update: Women’s Volleyball Survives Scare
articles.summary: Women’s soccer blanks Brown
articles.body:
The women's volleyball team fell in two sets to SMU at the Spikes Under The Lights exhibition last Thursday. The team looked rusty going up against a Mustangs team that had already played one match against a high-quality opponent the weekend before.

The Nittany Lions opened the regular season with three straight wins in the Penn State Invitational, but it did not always come easily. Penn State swept UConn and Hofstra but needed five sets to dispatch High Point on Sunday morning. Whitney Lauenstein and Kennedy Martin each reached double digit kills against Hofstra. The team defense was strong for most of the weekend, holding the three opponents to just .115 hitting percentage.

Penn State will face its first test of the season against Kentucky at Wrigley Field on Sunday (7pm on FOX) as part of the Big Ten-SEC Challenge. The Nittany Lions will then face DePaul on Monday (4pm on ESPNU).

Nicole Crane recorded her first career hat trick in the women's soccer team's 6-0 win over Brown on Sunday. MacKenzie Gress and Lily Selvy combined for a five-save shutout to help Penn State pick up its second win of the season and second straight shutout. It was an easy win for the team in its final tuneup game of the non-conference slate.

Penn State will host Virginia Tech tonight (5pm on Big Ten Plus) in the last non-conference game of the regular season.

The men's soccer team fell 2-1 to Pitt on Friday to drop to 1-2 on the season. Former Penn State midfielder Caden Grabfelder opened the scoring for Pitt on a penalty shot. Amadou Kone answered for Penn State shortly before halftime to even the score, but Anders Bordoy scored the game-winning goal for Pitt in the 54th minute. Penn State had no shots on goal in the second half, as the Pitt defense stifled the Nittany Lions' attack for most of the night.

Penn State will host Yale on Friday (7pm on Big Ten Plus). Tuesday's scheduled game against Bucknell was cancelled.

Penn State stormed back from a three-goal deficit in the fourth quarter against Virginia to force overtime, but the Cavaliers scored early in overtime to win 4-3. It was an admirable effort for Penn State in the first game of the Hannah Prince era. Olivia Marthins, Ella Gaitan, and Chloe Dhage all scored for the Nittany Lions in the opener.

The Nittany Lions responded with an easy 8-0 win over Lock Haven. Josephine Purdy was the only player to score twice in the game for Penn State as the Nittany Lions flexed their scoring depth. Lock Haven was held to just three shots on goal in the game.

Penn State will host Villanova on Friday (3pm on Big Ten Plus) and Delaware on Sunday (noon on Big Ten Plus).

articles.title: Review finds Russini-Vrabel bond violated standards at The Athletic
articles.summary: An investigation by The Athletic determined Dianna Russini violated news standards through a relationship with Mike Vrabel, the outlet said Thursday.
articles.body:
Sept. 3 (UPI) -- An investigation by The Athletic determined that former reporter Dianna Russini violated newsroom standards through her relationship with New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel, the outlet said Thursday.

The Athletic published the findings of the nearly five-month investigation under the headline: "Standards review of Dianna Russini's coverage for The Athletic."

Russini resigned from The New York Times Co.-owned outlet and was released from her contract April 14. The former senior insider for the NFL had taken the job role in August 2023.

The investigation, conducted by The Athletic's editorial director for standards and editorial quality Mike Semel, included a review of 903 stories and 77 videos published on the outlet's website.

It also included an examination of 204 episodes of the Scoop City podcast, which Russini co-hosted, and additional off-platform appearances she made while representing The Athletic.

Semel said he interviewed more than a dozen staff members from The Athletic who worked closely with Russini.

"Specifically, when it comes to The Athletic's standards, Russini was noncompliant," Semel wrote.

The Athletic said Russini reached out to executives at the outlet and the Times on April 7 to inform them about an impending article in the New York Post that would "suggest a romantic relationship" between Vrabel and Russini.

That same day, the Post's Page Six published an initial round of photos of the two, who are married to other people, showing them embracing and holding hands while at a luxury hotel in Sedona, Ariz.

The Athletic said that Russini waited two days before informing editors and managers about the upcoming photo release and then raised "issues of trust" when her explanation "did not align with facts." The Athletic's executive editor, Steven Ginsberg, initially called the photos "misleading" and said they lacked context.

Ginsberg later said additional information raised "new questions" in The Athletic's investigation.

Vrabel initially called it "laughable" to suggest his interaction with Russini was not a "completely innocent interaction." Russini said the initial round of photos didn't "represent the group of six people" she claimed were "hanging out" that day at the resort.

Semel said Russini "acknowledged a close relationship" with the Patriots coach, but "stressed that it was strictly professional." She also told executives that no additional "questionable pictures" would surface "because she had never done anything inappropriate," Semel wrote.

Additional photos, which showed Vrabel appearing the kiss Russini, were posted by Page Six on April 23. TMZ published another photo , which showed the duo at a Mississippi casino, on the same day.

Vrabel said that later that day that he took "accountability" for his actions that "caused a distraction" to the people he cares most about. He also said his actions did "not meet the standard" he holds himself to and opted to seek counseling. Vrabel did not attend the final day of the 2026 NFL Draft, held April 25 in Pittsburgh.

Semel said the published photos indicated a relationship, put the outlet's credibility in jeopardy and gave the "appearance of a conflict of interest."

"Russini's relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic's standards," Semel wrote. "Regardless of whether the relationship was romantic, it was a breach and should have been disclosed."

Semel said The Athletic did not complete an investigation about the "nature of the full relationship" between the former reporter and Vrabel.

The Athletic review "found no inaccuracies" from Russini in any of her stories that involved Vrabel or his teams. Semel recommended future safeguards for the outlet, including reviews between standards editor and newsroom employees during the onboarding process, clarity and enforcement of The Athletic's conflict of interest guidelines and sourcing standards.

articles.title: MSU QB Alessio Milivojevic Is Ready to Get Out of Practice and Into Game Time
articles.summary: A full offseason as QB1 changes everything. Alessio Milivojevic says the Spartans are done practicing against themselves and are ready for Friday night's ope...
articles.body:
Ahead of his first game as an opening-day starter, Michigan State quarterback Alessio Milivojevic spoke with the media about the team's readiness for Friday night's opener against Toledo , which is also Pat Fitzgerald's debut as head coach .

"There is excitement for every football game, but it just feels different," Milivojevic said in the SpartanMag video above. "It's hard to explain; I'm just ready to get back out there Friday and play."

With a roster that is mostly transfers and first-year players , the Spartans are looking to finally test themselves against a real opponent. They can practice together as much as they want, but they can't prove anything until game time.

"I think guys are just ready to go; the desire to get out there, you can feel it," Milivojevic said. "Guys are practicing 100% every day, ready to play someone other than our own team."

After going through training camp and the first half of last season as the backup, Milivojevic got a full offseason as the expected starter. Practicing with the other starters, instead of being plugged in halfway through the season , has made him more comfortable reading his receivers.

"Having the ability to prepare for an entire year, and then now go out and play with those guys you've been working with, helps build that camaraderie in an offense," Milivojevic said.

Milivojevic said he feels more confident in his overall command of the offense. Building experience with the reads and with his teammates over the last year has given him more confidence in himself and in the unit around him.

"Obviously there are guys that go out there and start with the first group, but I think that there are six or seven guys that can go out there and execute our offense," Milivojevic said. "I think the more receivers, the better you are off."

Milivojevic said he was happy to have offensive coordinator Nick Sheridan on the sideline during games. He likes being able to talk face-to-face about the game plan and the reads he's getting throughout the game, while the other offensive coaches watch from the booth and give the offense a second set of eyes.

After getting the last four starts of last season, Milivojevic saw the difference between practice and a full game. It's giving him a boost going into his first full season as the starter.

"The overall experience gives you a little confidence; you can practice as many times as you can, but I don't think anything is like a true live game," Milivojevic said.

articles.title: Panthers HC Dave Canales 'excited' over WR Tetairoa McMillan's offseason growth
articles.summary: Panthers HC Dave Canales praised WR Tetairoa McMillan for his growth, even literally, from this offseason.
articles.body:
As good as wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan looked in his first year with the Carolina Panthers , there was also a lot of room for improvement for the eventual Offensive Rookie of the Year .

The 6-foot-5, 212-pound McMillan had issues, at times, winning jump balls despite having superior size over the corners covering him. He also left a bit to desired when it came to contested catches and establishing his hand strength.

Well, the good news is that McMillan went out of his way to get bigger and stronger this offseason. Back in June, he told reporters he'd gained 17 pounds of muscle.

Here's what head coach Dave Canales had to say about McMillan's growth, per Joe Person at The Athletic , on Wednesday:

"He kinda was just a man on a mission to get stronger to be able to feel that power in his game. That really is a part of his game that needed to be addressed . . . He really wanted to do that and he attacked it, put on some good, solid mass. He's been great at the line of scrimmage, rugged to the ball. And he's still got all the same (other) stuff, so I'm excited to see him this year."

In theory, that extra muscle should help McMillan box out those smaller defensive backs in tight windows. It will also make tackling McMillan more difficult when he's attempting to add yards after the catch, an underrated part of his game.

McMillan proved to be a sharper route runner than advertised as a rookie—where he reeled in 70 passes for 1,014 yards and seven touchdowns. So if he can improve in that area as well, he could be in for a major boost to what was already an impressive skill set going into his second NFL campaign.

articles.title: Dayton Stivers football season back on, changing Cincinnati schedules
articles.summary: Just one day after cancelling the remainder of the 2026 football season, Dayton Stivers' season is back on. Here's what that means for Cincy teams.
articles.body:
Dayton Stivers School for the Arts abruptly changed course and will resume its 2026 football season.

After announcing the cancellation of Stivers's season on Monday, Aug. 31, Dayton Public Schools reversed the decision on Wednesday, Sept. 2, following a meeting with football parents.

"After listening to your concerns and suggestions, we've decided to move forward with the football season at Stivers School for the Arts. Thank you for your thoughtful, passionate comments in defense of your children and extracurricular activities," Superintendant David Lawrence said in a statement.

The season was initially cancelled due to low participation numbers and injuries. DPS will continue to monitor the situation to address player safety concerns.

Setting the scene - Week 2 football fans, bands, cheerleaders | Photos

Four Greater Cincinnati Schools were scheduled to play Stivers later this season. New Miami already replaced Stivers on the schedule with Preble Shawnee, playing later today, Sept. 3. Other future opponents included Shroder (Sept. 24), Norwood (Oct. 2), and Summit Country Day (Oct. 9).

Norwood athletic director Chuck Richardson III announced the school would honor the game against Stivers on Oct. 2.

Summit Country Day athletic director Greg Dennis confirmed that the team will still replace Stivers with a second matchup against Miami Valley Christian Academy on Oct. 9.

Shroder had not yet found a replacement game as of Sept. 2, and did not immediately respond to an inquiry about their updated scheduling plans.

Stivers competes in OHSAA Division V and is in just its second season after a being revived from a 40-year absence. The team went 2-8 last season, forfeiting one game. In the first game of the 2026 season Stivers lost to Gamble Montessori, 50-6. A week two game against Dunbar was cancelled.

One factor influencing DPS's decision to revive the season was the inability for Stivers players to continue the season with other Dayton Schools. Unlike Cincinnati's Lockland, which cancelled its season in early August, Stivers players were not eligible to play for neighboring schools. Since the season has already begun, OHSAA bylaw 4-1-4 considered the school to have sponsored the sport.

Families of the Stivers football team are expected to receive written plans for the remainder of the season sometime on Sept. 3.

articles.title: Kyle Schwarber reacts to Phillies’ biggest trade deadline acquisition
articles.summary: Philadelphia Phillies designated hitter Kyle Schwarber had some words on their trade deadline.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies, who looked dead in the water after a dreadful 9-19 start to the season, have rallied to within throwing distance of first place in the National League East. The club is 79-61, four games behind the first-place Atlanta Braves.

The two teams will battle it out in Philadelphia for a four-game series this weekend from Friday through Monday. They will then meet again in Atlanta next weekend for a three-game set.

Oddly enough, the Phillies and Braves have not played a series against each other since they also played twice in two weekends back in late April. The Braves took five of six, but that was before the Phillies and designated hitter Kyle Schwarber really got going.

Aug 23, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Phillies designated hitter Kyle Schwarber (12) flips his bat after hitting a walk-off home run during the ninth inning the St. Louis Cardinals at Citizens Bank Park. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The 33-year-old signed back with Philadelphia this past offseason on a five-year, $150 million contract. He has played in 134 games, slashing .240/.355/.517 (.872 OPS) with 40 home runs and 83 RBIs.

Schwarber's $30 million yearly price tag has been worth it for the club this year, as he has been exactly the type of hitter they have seen since his Phillies debut in 2022.

The Phillies were recently the subject of an article by Bob Nightengale of USA Today. In it, Schwarber spoke on new trade deadline acquisition Luis Arráez. He praised the second baseman heavily.

'"He just adds diversity to our lineup," Schwarber says, "and shows us that we can score runs in different ways. It doesn't have to be by the home run. It can be just putting balls in play, moving guys around. We've got a lot of tools in the bag now. You can see the difference he's made to our entire team."'

The 29-year-old is in his eighth MLB season, and has now suited up for five different teams, four in the last three seasons. He has crafted a fairly unique reputation in today's game of a low-strikeout, high-contact type of player.

The Phillies traded for him from the San Francisco Giants on Aug. 3 for an assortment of minor league pitching prospects. Since coming to Philadelphia, Arráez is slashing .280/.295/.383 (.678 OPS).

Though those numbers are down, he is driving in a good amount of runs and has only four strikeouts in 112 plate appearances. It is clear that his kind of approach is what they have needed in previous October runs.

articles.title: Three Rivers Report: Did the Steelers lie about Joey Porter Jr’s injury?

articles.summary: The Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets are coming off their best season in over a decade. That, combined with Deion Sanders coming to town has them about to do some...
articles.body:
The Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets are coming off their best season in over a decade. That, combined with Deion Sanders coming to town has them about to do something they haven't done in two decades: play their home opener in front of a sold out crowd.

According to the school , it's their first season opening sellout since Brady Quinn and the Notre Dame Fighting Irish came to town in 2006. Notre Dame won that game 14-10 . Calvin Johnson caught seven passes for 111 yards and scored the Yellow Jackets' only touchdown that day. It was so long ago that a senior tight end named Marcus Freeman caught a pass for the Irish.

It is also Georgia Tech's third straight sellout. They also filled the 52,113 seat Bobby Dowd Stadium in the final two games last season. It's the first time the school has had three straight sellouts since 2002.

Georgia Tech beat Colorado on the road in Week 1 last season, 27-20. They went on to win their first eight games before losing four of their last five. Still, coach Brent Key has people interested in Yellow Jackets football as he heads into his fifth season in charge.

While the possibility of winning games is certainly a great draw for the football team, you also can't ignore Coach Prime being involved. Despite the fact that he's coming off a 3-9 campaign, there's still a curiosity when the circus comes to town. There's also the possibility that the fans in Georgia just want to see how small the Colorado players are in person.

The game will be broadcast on ESPN at 8 p.m. ET. In addition to everything mentioned above, this will also mark Alberto Mendoza's debut as the Georgia Tech quarterback. The little brother of Heisman winner and No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza threw five touchdowns in mop-up duty lats season at Indiana.

articles.title: Fabio Wardley Admits He Was a ‘Victim of His Own Success’ in Daniel Dubois Defeat
articles.summary: Fabio Wardley has admitted that his fast start against Daniel Dubois worked against him as the heavyweight rivals prepare for […]
articles.body:
Fabio Wardley has admitted that his fast start against Daniel Dubois worked against him as the heavyweight rivals prepare for their October rematch. Wardley knocked Dubois down twice in their first fight at Manchester's Co-op Live Arena in May, but failed to finish the contest and was stopped in the 11th round. The result gave Dubois the WBO world title and handed Wardley the first defeat of his professional career.

Wardley said he had two clear chances to end the fight but became too comfortable after hurting Dubois early. The British heavyweight has now activated his rematch clause and will meet Dubois again on October 17 at The O2 in London, with Wardley promising a different response after what happened in their first fight.

Fabio Wardley Admits He Became Too Comfortable Against Daniel Dubois

Wardley dropped Dubois only 10 seconds into the fight. He scored another knockdown in the third round. Those moments gave Wardley chances to press for a stoppage, but he did not make the most of them.

"On two occasions I was literally a few seconds away from winning the fight," Wardley said. "I could have capitalised on those moments better, could have done a bit more with them, could have pressed the action a bit better."

The 31-year-old said his early success changed how he approached the fight.

"I became a victim of my own success," he admitted. "I got too comfortable with the fact that I caught him in the first 10 seconds of the fight."

Wardley expected another opening instead of forcing the finish. Dubois survived the early pressure, recovered and eventually stopped Wardley in the 11th round.

Daniel Dubois Survived Two Knockdowns Before Winning the Fight

Daniel Dubois recovered after the two knockdowns and changed the direction of the contest. Wardley acknowledged that Dubois handled the pressure and continued fighting.

"To his credit, he turned it around. He weathered the storm. He picked himself back up and he powered through," Wardley said.

Wardley also rejected claims that referee Howard Foster should have stopped the fight earlier because of the damage to his face. Wardley had swelling, cuts and blood during the later rounds, but he said he remained able to continue.

"I would have protested anything before the final bell because I was still on my feet," Wardley said. "A lot of people read a lot into the aesthetic of some bruising, a cut and some blood mixed with sweat."

The Daniel Dubois fight therefore continued until the 11th round, when Dubois stopped Wardley and claimed the WBO world title.

Fabio Wardley Confirms October Rematch With Daniel Dubois

Fabio Wardley activated his rematch clause after the defeat, setting up another Daniel Dubois fight on October 17 at The O2 in London.

The short gap between the two fights has raised questions about Wardley's condition, but he said he and his team know he is ready.

"No one knows me better than me… and the team I've had around me from the beginning," he said. "We know that I'm ready. We know that I'm fighting fit. The only way to silence that narrative is by the performance on the night."

Wardley has also refused to blame anyone for his defeat.

"I have zero excuses for the loss on the night and zero excuses going into the rematch," he said at the launch press conference. "It's just another chapter in the story that is my career."

Daniel Dubois enters the rematch as the WBO world champion, while Fabio Wardley will look to respond differently after his first professional loss.

Real Madrid defender Raul Asencio has spoken publicly for the first time since being acquitted in the case involving the distribution of a video containing sexual content involving minors.

The Spanish defender was acquitted by the court earlier today after he issued an apology to the victims while also paying compensation.

This comes at a time when the La Fabrica graduate is also under the scanner after being convicted for driving under the influence of alcohol .

Asencio has now issued a statement on social media following his acquittal in the trial over the distribution of the video.

The two victims formally forgave the four Real Madrid players who had been prosecuted, including Asencio.

The defender used his statement to respond to comments made by his manager, José Mourinho, and made clear that he now wants to have his say both on and off the pitch.

"Now it's my turn to speak, and not only on the pitch, but also away from it," Asencio wrote.

Asencio explained that the months-long process had been difficult, particularly as reports and opinions about him were published before the courts had reached a decision.

"Today, after a long period of silence and respecting a legal process in which I always had faith, I can say that I have been ACQUITTED. I believe the time has come to share a few words.

"Over these past few months I have experienced a difficult situation and, at times, I have had to see information and opinions about me published before the Justice system had ruled.

"I understand and respect the work of the media in reporting and expressing opinions, but I also believe it is important to remember that behind every story there is a person and a family who live with the consequences of everything that is published.

"I have always trusted that justice would eventually put things right. Today there is a judicial ruling that speaks for itself, and I accept it calmly and with the satisfaction of being able to close a chapter that has been extremely important to me."

Rather than focusing on the criticism he received, Asencio said he wanted to remember the people who stood by him throughout the process.

"I don't want to hold on to the noise or the difficult moments. I prefer to remember the support of the people who stood by me and trusted me throughout this time.

"I want to sincerely thank my family, my friends, my agent, my lawyers and everyone who supported me and gave me strength when I needed it most."

Asencio also apologised for drunk-driving incident. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

"I also want to thank Real Madrid and everyone at the club who showed their confidence in me and allowed me to continue working, developing and enjoying what I love most: playing football.

"Throughout this process, I tried to stay away from it all, work and keep moving forward. Today I can do so with the peace of mind that I always believed in the truth."

Asencio also addresses the drink-driving incident

The Real Madrid defender also referred to the separate drink-driving incident for which he was punished, while the club is also investigating the matter.

"I also want to address an incident involving drink-driving. I am deeply sorry for what happened and I fully accept responsibility. It has been an experience from which I have learned, and I am absolutely clear that it will never happen again.

" Now I want to look ahead, keep working, keep developing and focus on what I love most: playing football. "

Asencio called on those who had spoken about him during the case to give the court's decision the same level of attention.

"To those who spoke about me during these months, I only ask that now the Justice system has given its ruling, this part of the story can also be told with the same attention.

"I don't want to get involved in controversies or look back. I want to close this chapter with respect, with my head held high and with a great desire to move forward.

"Now it's my turn to speak. And I completely agree with my coach: not only on the pitch, but also away from it.

" Hala Madrid . Let nobody have the slightest doubt," he concluded.

articles.title: San Diego Wave in talks with Juventus over Barbara Bonansea loan
articles.summary: San Diego Wave and Juventus are in negotiations regarding a season-long loan for Barbara Bonansea until June 2027. The 35-year-old’s contract is due to expir...
articles.body:
San Diego Wave and Juventus are in negotiations regarding a season-long loan for Barbara Bonansea until June 2027.

The 35-year-old's contract is due to expire next summer but discussions are under way regarding a contract extension that would keep the forward at the Italian club until June 2028. Nothing has been agreed yet.

A highly experienced player, Bonansea has been a mainstay for Juventus, amassing over 200 appearances, winning 15 trophies, including six Serie A league titles across nine seasons. Juventus have just qualified for the league phase of the Champions League and start their domestic campaign later this month.

On the international stage, Bonansea represented Italy at the 2019 World Cup and the 2025 European Championships, opening the scoring against England in the semi-final.

The loan move, managed by the same agency A&V sports, is similar to fellow Italy international Cristiana Girelli who joined Bay FC in February and has had her loan extended until next summer.

Bonansea would bolster San Diego's squad with eight games of the regular season left to play. As of Sunday, San Diego Wave named four players – Trinity Armstrong, Dudinha, Cat Macario and Kiki Pickett – on their injury list.

The club has remained one of the more consistent teams in the NWSL this year, floating at the top of the table. They sit 4th in the NWSL, level on points with Utah Royals in third, and eight points clear of Seattle Reign who occupy the last play-off spot in eighth.

Bonansea would join players like 23-year-old Trinity Byars who has had a standout season and is in contention for this year's golden boot race, tied with Washington Spirit's Trinity Rodman on 10 goals and just five shy of league-leading Ashley Sanchez.

articles.title: La Fórmula 1 del mar desembarca en Valencia: "La gente se va a sorprender"
articles.standfirst: Toma el relevo de Cádiz, sede española las últimas cuatro ediciones de SailGP. Se han vendido todas las entradas para la grada Marea Roja
articles.summary: Toma el relevo de Cádiz, sede española las últimas cuatro ediciones de SailGP. Se han vendido todas las entradas para la grada Marea Roja
articles.body: Valencia vuelve a ser capital mundial de la vela. La ciudad que acogió dos ediciones de la Copa América (2007 y 2010) ha visto volar este jueves en sus aguas por primera vez –durante el entrenamiento oficial– a la flota del Rolex SailGP Championship, la liga de catamaranes voladores que pueden superar los 100 km/h. De hecho, el récord de velocidad lo estableció el equipo francés en Sassnitz en el último Gran Premio (107,63 km/h). Un total de 115 contenedores han sido trasladados a Marina Port València para montar toda la infraestructura necesaria para la competición. La zona se ha transformado en un ‘paddock’ que, por temas logísticos, está dividido en dos bases donde se reparten los 13 equipos, entre ellos ‘Los Gallos’ españoles liderados por los campeones olímpicos Diego Botín y Florian Trittel. Los anfitriones llegan segundos en la clasificación general, a 14 puntos de Australia y en la mejor temporada de su vida en la que ha hecho siete podios en los siete Grandes Premios que han navegado. En los otros dos, por problemas técnicos, no compitieron. Valencia toma el relevo de Cádiz, la sede del Gran Premio de España los últimos cuatro años. “Cádiz fue espectacular, pero se nos quedó pequeña porque SailGP ha crecido mucho. En Valencia sí hay espacio para montar el estadio, que es nuestro ADN. La gente va a ver a los barcos súper cerca y se va a sorprender. Queremos abrir la vela a todo el mundo, hacer que la gente a la que le gusta el motor y la velocidad nos siga. Tenemos un estadio, hay gradas y los barcos te pasan por delante y casi te mojan. No somos un evento de vela, somos un evento de entretenimiento”, señala Alejandra Mato, jefa de gabinete de SailGP y mano derecha de Russell Coutts, el CEO. Y para ver los barcos tan cerca se ha montado en la Marina Port Valencia una gigantesca grada que cuenta con capacidad para albergar a unos 9.000 espectadores que verán competir oeste fin de semana a los 13 espectaculares F50 repartidos en dos flotas y volando sobre sus foils (hidroalas). “En la Grada Marea Roja está todo vendido. Hay mucha ilusión en la ciudad por vernos y nosotros también estamos muy ilusionados con este Gran Premio de España y con ganas de hacer disfrutar a la gente”, dice Florian Trittel, trimmer de ala de ‘Los Gallos’ con una sonrisa. “Cádiz va a estar siempre en nuestras raíces como equipo, pero Valencia es una ciudad con una historia náutica muy fuerte y de más fácil acceso para venir a ver el evento. Puede ser un Gran Premio increíble”, augura Diego Botín. Quien mejor la conoce es Joan Cardona, bronce olímpico en Tokio 2020 y que precisamente se preparó para esa cita en aguas valencianas durante dos años. “Valencia es una ciudad de diez. El campo de regatas favorece mucho que la grada esté paralela con la dirección del viento y el espectador pueda ver la competición mejor. Si le sumas la gastronomía y la temperatura tiene todos los ingredientes para ser un grandísimo evento”, asegura el táctico y grinder.

articles.title: Clemson Or LSU? Ole Miss Handles Louisville? Joel Klatt's Week 1 CFB Picks
articles.summary: Joel Klatt gives his picks for Week 1 of the college football season, featuring Clemson-LSU, Louisville-Ole Miss and Boise State-Oregon.
articles.body: "Showtime!" Week 1 of the 2026 college football season commences on Thursday night, kicking off a five-day slate where at least one game is played across the sport. FOX Sports' Lead College Football Analyst, Joel Klatt, shared his picks for the biggest games of the week on the latest episode of "The Joel Klatt Podcast." LSU 31, Clemson 14 Klatt's Thoughts: "This [LSU] defense really should be able to shut down Clemson in this matchup. You've got [defensive coordinator] Blake Baker back. Princewill Umanmielen transfers with Lane Kiffin from Ole Miss. This guy's an excellent defensive end. They're talented out there. You got [linebacker] Whit Weeks. This is a good team. You got Sam Leavitt, an experienced quarterback. … Lane always has a good offense. This team should be good. They should be ready to go, and it comes down to execution. How quickly can they learn this system and execute? "Baker has been there before, so it shouldn't take that long for these guys to really get acquainted with this defense, and that's where I think that they dominate this game." Klatt's Pick: "In that environment, with that type of energy, I like LSU, 31-14." Ole Miss 30, Louisville 21 Klatt's Thoughts: "It could look sloppy, at times, and we'll see if Louisville can take advantage. Louisville has been a team that has constantly defeated really good opponents like Miami and JMU. When [head coach] Jeff Brohm was at Purdue, he was really the "Spoilermaker." They know how to do this, but I do think Ole Miss, in the end, is going to have too much because I think Trinidad Chambliss is the most unique quarterback in the country in that he's the most threatening both outside of the pocket and inside the pocket. "That's going to be very difficult for Louisville and its new defensive coordinator [Mark Ivey and Steve Ellis are co-coordinators] to deal with. He's [Chambliss] so dynamic." Klatt's Pick: "I think Ole Miss wins the game, 30-21." Oregon 42, Boise State 13 Klatt's Thoughts: "I think Oregon is further along in its build under Dan Lanning than Boise State. They've got more purpose and more urgency with these guys coming back. They've got an experienced quarterback in Dante Moore. I believe they can be explosive on offense, and I think they're going to be absolutely suffocating on defense. The one question I have for Oregon is at offensive coordinator. Drew Mehringer comes in as a promotion from within to replace Will Stein [at offensive coordinator]. We'll see how he does. I want to see the offense and how it works, very similarly to Ole Miss. "Boise State had a great pass defense a year ago, but it lost four of its five defensive backs from a year ago. Oregon should really control this game. If they can't control the game with their offense, they should be able to control the game with their defense, and, more specifically, its defensive line. … think about purpose, think about urgency, think about what this team is actually there to do, and it's not just go out there and struggle against Boise State." Klatt's Pick: "I like Oregon in this one, 42-13."

articles.title: SEC sues LSU, alleging a coordinated push to recruit ex-pro athletes in defiance of rules
articles.summary: The Southeastern Conference filed a lawsuit against LSU and its leadership in Alabama federal court on Thursday, alleging the school had “waged a deliberate and coordinated campaign to recruit professional athletes” against league rules.
articles.body: BATON ROUGE, La. — The Southeastern Conference filed a lawsuit against LSU and its leadership in Alabama federal court on Thursday, alleging the school had “waged a deliberate and coordinated campaign to recruit professional athletes” against league rules. The extraordinary step against one of the league’s founding members in 1933 came as SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey testified 400 miles away in a courtroom not far from Tiger Stadium, defending the league’s ability to enforce its rules as several dozen athletes try to play this fall after they turned pro. Former New Orleans Saints defensive lineman Zxavian Harris and former Cleveland Browns tight end Dae’Quan Wright sat next to each other in the gallery as the hearing began, with Sankey taking the stand a short time later.. At least seven bailiffs were on hand. The lawsuit asks for a court injunction barring LSU from violating the SEC’s First Amendment rights by forcing it to “associate with conduct that is contrary to the conference’s purpose and mission.” It was filed in northern Alabama because the SEC is based in Birmingham. Attorneys for the athletes, the NCAA and the SEC were appearing before East Baton Rouge Parish Judge William Jorden, who scheduled the hearing concerning the status of his earlier temporary injunction preventing the NCAA from ruling recent former pros or fifth-year college athletes ineligible — a stance also taken by the SEC and other Power Four conferences with formal rules adopted last week. Jorden also wanted the NCAA to explain why it should not be held in contempt after the power conferences set up potential punishments of its member schools who place former NFL or NBA athletes on their football or basketball rosters. The players in question also include former Denver Broncos defensive back Blake Cotton, who like Harris and Wright is hoping to join LSU and new coach Lane Kiffin. Wright, who played for Kiffin last season at Mississippi, started practicing with at LSU this week, too late to be eligible for Saturday’s home opener against Clemson under the NCAA’s required seven days of practice. Harris, who also played at Ole Miss last season, has committed to LSU, while Cotton, who played at Utah last fall, has been recruited by Kiffin. All three are among a host of athletes who’ve argued in lawsuits around the country that they are unfairly being denied an opportunity to spend a fifth year in college under newly adopted NCAA rules allowing for five full years of competition. In all, the NCAA says there are approximately 450 athlete plaintiffs seeking additional eligibility through litigation, with some 300 of them winning the ability to play at least for now and about 150 who have been rejected. The athletes in the case who signed pro contracts have argued they did so only because current rules that would have allowed them another college season weren’t adopted until after their decisions to leave for the chance to make an NFL roster. The SEC filed a brief in the case on Wednesday in which it stated that the question before the judge should be a narrow one regarding whether the conference “can enforce and require its member institutions to comply with SEC rules.” The SEC’s proposed punishments include significant fines, up to half-season suspensions for coaches and member universities’ loss of voting on privileges on league business matters. Sankey provided an affidavit stating that SEC university presidents voted 15-0 in favor of the new rules, with LSU’s Wade Rousse abstaining. Sankey also said the SEC was acting on its own and not attempting to collude with NCAA to stop Kiffin from bringing in ex-pros. The fight over eligibility between schools and their own conference s and the NCAA has simmered for months and spilled into politics. Georgia Attorney General Chris Carr reportedly sent a letter of support to Sankey, encouraging him to take “all measures available” to punish LSU if it added former NFL players to its 2026 roster of 105 players, which was due to be submitted to the SEC by Friday. He also criticized the judge’s injunction. “It is no coincidence that the very institution set to potentially use this temporary order to flout the SEC’s rule is in the trial court’s own backyard,” Carr wrote. Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill also weighed in, writing in a brief that the NCAA had subjected athletes in the case to a “classic bait-and-switch.” “The NCAA’s ever-changing rules have consequences beyond these individual athletes,” said Murrill, who attended the hearing and chatted with plaintiff attorneys before the proceeding. “They affect the universities that recruit them, the other student-athletes with whom they compete, and the coaches and administrators responsible for complying with an increasingly complicated set of rules.”
