articles.title: Ranking the Worst Trades in Sports This Century
articles.summary: For every elated fanbase that welcomes a new star to town, there's an equally downtrodden group absorbing the gut punch of a beloved player being ripped from their favorite team. In return, they're often left with little more than several question marks in matching jerseys.
articles.body:
For every elated fanbase that welcomes a new star to town, there's an equally downtrodden group absorbing the gut punch of a beloved player being ripped from their favorite team. In return, they're often left with little more than several question marks in matching jerseys.

Even in an era when sports are broken down to the smallest minutiae through analytics and media scrutiny, these one-sided deals still happen somewhat frequently.

Just ask Los Angeles Clippers fans how they feel after learning that the Kawhi Leonard salary-cap circumvention scandal will cost them five first-round picks.

Boston fans are no stranger to this phenomenon, either, with Mookie Betts getting shipped out in 2020 and Jaylen Brown being sent to a hated rival six years later.

Here, we've ranked the worst one-sided blockbusters since the year 2000. But we didn't just look at how the trades appeared on paper at the time. Instead, we factored in:

Immediate perception : Did the deal look lopsided from the start?

Long-term impact : How did it shape the teams' futures, on and off the field/court/ice?

Superstar value : Were Hall of Fame-caliber players or franchise cornerstones involved?

Cultural/market shock : Did the trade shake the sport beyond just wins and losses?

While we know how many of these deals aged over the years, a handful are still relatively fresh. We can only judge those based on compensation and immediate reaction.

The trade: Tennessee sent A.J. Brown to Philadelphia for a 2022 first-round pick (No. 18 overall) and a 2022 third-round pick (No. 101 overall).

The Titans traded Brown because they did not want to sign him to a long-term extension. The Eagles happily stepped in.

Brown immediately blossomed into Jalen Hurts' top weapon and turned Philadelphia into one of the league's most dangerous offenses. His physical dominance and ability to stretch defenses gave the Eagles the kind of No. 1 receiver that changes an entire unit. In his first three years in Philly, the Eagles went to two Super Bowls and won one.

Meanwhile, Tennessee spent the No. 18 overall pick on Burks, who failed to pan out. After three injury-ravaged, ineffective seasons, the Titans waived him in late July 2025.

This was a case of moving on from a proven star in his prime for draft picks that offered only potential. The Eagles capitalized instantly, while the Titans moved backward.

Even though Brown pushed his way out of Philly in 2026, the Eagles got a first-round pick from the New England Patriots in return. So in essence, the Eagles traded a first-round pick for Brown, got two Super Bowl appearances and one championship with him, and then flipped him for a first-round pick four years after trading for him in the first place.

This isn't the ugliest trade on our list, but its impact was immediately apparent. Just ask the Kansas City Chiefs.

The trade: Washington sent Juan Soto and Josh Bell to San Diego for a package including CJ Abrams, MacKenzie Gore, James Wood and Robert Hassell III.

At the time, San Diego looked like it had secured the biggest star of his generation. Soto's bat was already historic, and adding him gave the Padres one of the most feared lineups in baseball.

However, the Padres never turned that firepower into postseason glory. They wound up trading Soto to the Yankees less than 18 months after acquiring him. Meanwhile, the Nationals built a promising young core with Abrams, Gore and Wood, who have already started producing in the majors.

While the Soto era in San Diego was exciting, the long-term imbalance is clear. The Nationals gained controllable talent to set up their future, while the Padres made a short-term splash and have little to show for it today.

This is not the most lopsided deal in recent memory because Soto is still great, but the imbalance between future-building and fleeting stardom heavily favors Washington.

The trade: San Antonio sent Kawhi Leonard and Danny Green to Toronto for DeMar DeRozan, Jakob Poeltl and a protected 2019 first-round pick.

This trade completely reshaped the modern NBA landscape.

Even though Leonard only had one year left on his contract, the Raptors gambled on him. That decision paid off handsomely. Kawhi delivered one of the greatest postseason runs in modern history and guided the Raptors to their first-ever NBA championship in 2019, although he left in free agency that summer.

Meanwhile, the Spurs received DeRozan, a proven scorer whose arrival coincided with the end of their NBA-record 22-year streak of playoff appearances in 2020. Poeltl became a solid starting center (who ironically is now back with the Raptors), but neither player replaced Leonard's Hall-of-Fame shot-making.

This deal shows how one bold move can redefine a franchise's history. Toronto gave up a fan favorite in DeRozan, but the reward was immortality. That experience also helped lure Leonard back to Toronto in 2026.

While Toronto clearly won this deal, San Antonio at least got rotation pieces, unlike trades above this spot where the return was essentially worthless.

The trade: Dallas sent edge-rusher Micah Parsons to Green Bay for Kenny Clark, a 2026 first-round pick and a 2027 first-round pick.

It's still early, but it sure looks like the Packers fleeced the Cowboys.

Parsons is one of the NFL's most destructive defenders. He collapses pockets and single-handedly disrupts offenses with his edge-rushing prowess. The Cowboys got back Kenny Clark, who's a dependable interior lineman but is nowhere near Parsons' tier.

The two future first-rounders that Dallas got for Parsons are wild cards for now. They could end up being lottery tickets that could swing the narrative on this deal years from now. But there's little chance that the Cowboys will end up drafting a player of Parsons' caliber with either of those picks.

For now, the Packers look like clear winners of the Parsons trade, even though he tore his ACL late in his first season in Green Bay and is set to miss the start of the 2026 campaign. This wasn't Herschel Walker-level bad, but the optics add fuel to the fire of Dallas sports.

The trade: Boston sent Mookie Betts and David Price to the Dodgers for Alex Verdugo, Jeter Downs and Connor Wong.

The Red Sox traded Betts to shed salary. That decision will never stop stinging.

Betts was an MVP in his prime, a five-tool superstar who could anchor a franchise. The Dodgers got exactly that. He's already helped them win three World Series, provided MVP-level seasons and became a face of one of baseball's most successful organizations.

Meanwhile, Boston received a package that produced almost nothing. Verdugo had flashes but never lived up to expectations. Downs did not pan out. Wong has been serviceable but nothing special.

This deal will forever be remembered as a cautionary tale of prioritizing finances over talent.

The trade: Toronto sent Bargnani to New York for Steve Novak, Marcus Camby, Quentin Richardson, a 2014 second-round pick, a 2016 first-round pick and a 2017 second-round pick.

Knicks fans swear by the adage "Once a Knick, always a Knick." Andrea Bargnani may be the only former player to whom that adage doesn't apply.

Bargnani was supposed to be "Dirk-lite" in New York next to Carmelo Anthony. Instead, he nearly undid a decade of Nowitzki's work to reverse the "soft Euro" label.

Bargnani barely contributed, his contract was a burden, and New York essentially handed Toronto the flexibility to reset with a pick that became Jakob Poeltl.

The Italian bust's tenure in New York can be remembered in a single sequence. Bargnani lumbered toward the rim, only to be greeted by two Sixers who barely broke a sweat swatting him back to reality. Bargnani crashed down, injuring himself and punctuating the play with the kind of unintentional comedy that defined his Knicks tenure.

The trade: Miami traded Wes Welker for a 2007 second-round pick and a 2007 seventh-round pick.

The Patriots saw what Miami did not: Welker's ability to dominate from the slot. In New England, he became the prototype for modern slot receivers.

With Tom Brady under center, Welker racked up five 100-plus-catch seasons, providing reliability and production unmatched at the time. He led the league in receptions three times over a five-year span, while Miami got almost nothing of value in return.

Samson Satele, whom the Dolphins selected with the second-round pick that they got in this trade, lasted only two years before they sent him to the then-Oakland Raiders. Abraham Knight, their seventh-round pick, never played a single regular-season snap for them.

Welker was transformative for the Patriots' offense. His ability to move the chains changed drives and seasons. Miami effectively gave a division rival the weapon that kept its dynasty going.

The trade: New York acquired Eddy Curry, Antonio Davis and a 2006 first-round pick from Chicago for Tim Thomas, Mike Sweetney, Jermaine Jackson, a 2006 first-rounder, a 2007 first-rounder, a 2007 second-rounder, and a 2009 second-rounder.

It must be said: This is not about Eddy Curry. The center was a talented big man and by all accounts a good person. It is about the draft picks.

Before the trade, Curry had missed time with a heart condition and declined to undergo DNA testing that might have revealed serious long-term risks. Rather than back out on the deal, Knicks general manager Isiah Thomas mortgaged the team's future by sending out multiple first-round picks for him. (Those two first-rounders became LaMarcus Aldridge and Joakim Noah).

Curry had one solid season in New York, but weight issues and injuries quickly turned the deal into a dead end. It didn't help that Thomas' roster construction made it impossible for any player to thrive in that era for the Knicks.

While the draft price was steep, the long-term damage was more about wasted picks than a superstar giveaway. That keeps it below the truly franchise-changing trades higher up in these rankings.

The trade: Oakland sent Randy Moss to New England for a 2007 fourth-round pick.

The Raiders gave up on one of the greatest receivers of all time at his lowest point. The Patriots recognized that the talent was still there. What followed was the most explosive offense the NFL had ever seen.

Moss and Tom Brady broke records in 2007, coming one win shy of a perfect season. He hauled in a single-season-record 23 catches that year and led the NFL with 13 touchdown receptions two years later as well.

Meanwhile, the Raiders spent the fourth-round pick that they got for Moss on defensive back John Bowie, who played only five regular-season games for them.

It's one thing to lose a trade. It's another to gift a cornerstone to the league's reigning dynasty. This was a masterpiece for New England and a disaster for Oakland.

The trade: Washington sent Filip Forsberg to Nashville for Martin Erat and Michael Latta.

This is widely known as one of the worst trades in NHL history.

Forsberg became a perennial 30-goal scorer, the kind of winger who can anchor a franchise, while the Capitals effectively got nothing. Erat lasted less than a year in Washington, and Latta was irrelevant.

The Predators essentially received a franchise cornerstone for spare parts. The imbalance is a textbook case of why patience with young talent is critical.

The Forsberg trade ranks ahead of the Moss deal because Washington received two players who provided zero impact, while Oakland at least moved on from a frustrated veteran.

The trade: Cleveland traded Trent Richardson to Indianapolis for a 2014 first-round pick.

Richardson averaged only 3.6 yards per carry as a rookie, but the Colts gambled on his draft pedigree. The result was one of the biggest busts of the era.

The 2012 No. 3 overall pick lasted less than two years in Indianapolis. He had 316 carries for only 977 yards (3.1 yards per carry) and six touchdowns during his time with the Colts.

The Browns at least got a first-rounder in exchange for Richardson, which is remarkable considering his trajectory. They did not make the most of it, but cashing in when they did gave them a rare win.

For Indianapolis, this was a costly swing that wasted resources during Andrew Luck's prime years. It was the definition of buying high and selling low.

The imbalance went beyond production. It was about opportunity cost.

The trade: Seattle sent Russell Wilson and a 2022 fourth-round pick to Denver for Drew Lock, Noah Fant, Shelby Harris, a 2022 first-round pick, a 2022 second-round pick, a 2022 fifth-round pick, a 2023 first-round pick and a 2023 second-round pick.

This one unraveled faster than anyone expected.

The Broncos thought they were getting the final piece to compete for a Super Bowl. Instead, Wilson struggled from the outset. The offense never clicked, coaches came and went, and the five-year, $240-plus million contract extension that he signed after the trade made things worse.

Denver gave up premium draft capital and had little to show for it. Meanwhile, Seattle used those picks to restock quickly. Devon Witherspoon and Charles Cross, whom the Seahawks selected with the first-round picks that they got from the Broncos, became foundational players.

The Wilson era in Denver will be defined by lackluster play, a bungled final season, a lopsided trade, and a fortune wasted to remain stuck in the quarterback void.

The trade: The Thunder dealt James Harden, Cole Aldrich, Daequan Cook and Lazar Hayward to the Rockets for Kevin Martin, Jeremy Lamb, a 2013 first-round pick, a 2013 second-round pick and a 2014 first-round pick.

This one hurts because it killed a dynasty before it ever fully got off the ground.

Oklahoma City had three future MVPs in Kevin Durant, Russell Westbrook and Harden, all of whom were in their mid-20s. However, Harden wouldn't take a slightly below-max extension , so the Thunder decided to trade him to the Rockets.

Harden earned eight straight All-Star nods in Houston while leading the league in scoring three times and winning MVP in 2017-18. He brought the Rockets to the Western Conference Finals twice, although they were felled by Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors both times.

The Thunder only received role players in return for Harden, none of whom came close to replicating his production. Few trades are this haunting.

The Thunder likely would have won a championship had they prioritized signing Harden over Serge Ibaka. We could have been looking at a potential dynasty. Instead, they altered the course of the NBA by sending him to the Rockets.

The Harden trade ranks above the Moss and Forsberg deals because the Thunder had the chance to build a dynasty, but they chose money over legacy. The long-term ripple effects across the league make it even more damaging.

The trade: Miami traded Cabrera and Dontrelle Willis to Detroit for Dallas Trahern, Burke Badenhop, Frankie De La Cruz, Cameron Maybin, Andrew Miller and Mike Rabelo.

Detroit landed one of the greatest hitters of the 21st century. Cabrera won a Triple Crown along with a pair of MVPs and led the Tigers to deep playoff runs. The Marlins got six prospects, none of whom made a major impact.

It's one thing to trade a star. It's another to give away a Hall of Fame bat in his prime effectively for nothing.

This deal is a staple in lopsided trade conversations because the gap between Cabrera's career and what Miami got in return is pathetic in scale.

The Cabrera trade edges ahead of the Harden deal since OKC at least netted role players in the Harden trade. Miami's entire return collapsed. It was a complete miss for an all-time hitter.

The trade: Boston sent Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia for Paul George, two first-round picks and two second-round picks.

The Philadelphia 76ers eliminated the Boston Celtics in the first round of the 2026 playoffs in a heated seven-game series. Less than two months later, the Celtics traded Brown to the Sixers for a surprisingly meager return.

Brown is fresh off a career year in which he averaged 28.7 points, 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists. He helped Boston win 56 games and finish as the East's second seed while Jayson Tatum missed most of the season rehabbing a torn Achilles.

Brown is a five-time All-Star, a two-time All-NBA selection and was named Finals MVP during the Celtics' run to the 2024 championship. In return for him, Boston got back a washed 36-year-old who can't stay healthy, two first-round picks and "optionality."

Celtics president Brad Stevens said the team's path "looked a little bit more challenging with 70 percent of our cap and such a high percentage of our usage tied into two players." That's defensible. But did Boston have to trade Brown to a division rival?

Trading a co-star to a random contender stings. Trading him to the rival who eliminated you—and one you'll play four times a year—takes a special kind of front-office cockiness. Even Brown seemed thrown by it.

Boston had reportedly been shopping Brown for Giannis Antetokounmpo weeks earlier. The Celtics aimed for a superstar swap and settled for handing a division rival exactly what it needed to get scarier.

The picks might age well. But this decision never will.

The trade: The Celtics traded the 2017 No. 1 overall pick (Fultz) to the Sixers for the No. 3 overall pick (Tatum) and the Sacramento Kings' 2019 first-round pick.

Let's take a moment of silence to contemplate how Jayson Tatum and Joel Embiid would look together in Philly. OK, now back to reality.

Embiid's health has hampered him in recents seasons after a decade-plus of carrying the Sixers offensively. Fultz remains unsigned and out of the league. Meanwhile, Tatum has reached the NBA Finals twice and won a championship in 2024.

In exchange for Tatum and a future first-round pick, Philadelphia wound up with a player whose broken jumper defined his tenure and left the organization with nothing but regret. What makes this misstep so painful for Philadelphia is how avoidable it was.

The Sixers had a clear path to pair Embiid with another superstar, which could have given them the best duo in the league for a decade. Instead, then-Celtics president Danny Ainge took advantage of a bumbling front office and landed one of the best future Celtics of all time.

Given the long-term fallout for both franchises, this deal continues to age worse and worse. The only silver lining for the Sixers is that they eventually traded Fultz for the pick that they'd spend on Tyrese Maxey.

The trade: Houston dealt Deshaun Watson and a 2024 sixth-round pick to Cleveland for a 2022 first-round pick, a 2022 fourth-round pick, a 2023 first-round pick, a 2023 third-round pick, a 2024 first-round pick and a 2024 fourth-round pick.

Deshaun Watson missed the entire 2021 season after nearly two dozen women filed lawsuits accusing him of sexual misconduct or harassment. That didn't stop the Browns from trading a package including three first-round picks for him, though. Not only that, but they also gave him the largest guaranteed contract in NFL history (five years, $230 million) as part of the trade.

That backfired spectacularly. Watson was suspended for 11 games in 2022 and has scuffled through injury-ravaged seasons since. He's currently recovering from a torn Achilles, and it appears unlikely that he'll ever play another snap for Cleveland.

In March 2025, Browns owner Jimmy Haslam conceded the trade was a "big swing-and-miss." Meanwhile, the picks they sent to Houston helped the Texans establish the foundation for their quick rise out of the rebuilding ashes.

The Browns' desperation to find a franchise quarterback led them to trade for Watson despite his off-field issues, which could haunt them for years to come. The volume of picks the Browns gave up and the fully guaranteed contract they gave Watson made it arguably the worst NFL trade in recent memory, which is why we have it in the top five here.

3. Kevin Garnett and Paul Pierce to the Nets

The trade: The Celtics traded Kevin Garnett, Paul Pierce, Jason Terry, D.J. White and a 2017 second-round pick for Keith Bogans, MarShon Brooks, Kris Humphries, Kris Joseph, Gerald Wallace, a 2014 first-round pick, a 2016 first-round pick, a 2017 first-round pick swap and a 2018 first-round pick.

A decade later, everyone knows how this trade turned out. The Celtics rebuilt around those picks, eventually landing the superstar tandem of Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum, who powered them to a championship in 2024. Meanwhile, Brooklyn got one playoff run with KG and Pierce and then fell into years of irrelevance.

The Nets mortgaged their future for aging stars who were way past their prime. There's a reason why Danny Ainge has the reputation he does as the league's most difficult negotiator. He really kicks you when you're down in trade negotiations.

Garnett and Pierce were shells of themselves in Brooklyn, where they teamed up with Brook Lopez, Deron Williams and Joe Johnson in an era where front offices would try to cram as many big names onto a roster as possible. Meanwhile, Boston played the long game, building around its star wings with depth and defense.

This deal ranks above the Fultz/Tatum swap because Boston used the Nets' picks to build an entire new era that ended up winning a championship. Philly's mistake hurt, but Brooklyn ushered in its own collapse while setting the Celtics up for a title.

The trade: Dallas sent Luka Dončić, Maxi Kleber and Markieff Morris to the Lakers for Anthony Davis, Max Christie and a 2029 first-round pick.

You knew this was coming. Nico Harrison's ineptitude is as inevitable as Thanos.

This deal was shocking on every level. Luka was 25 and already a generational superstar. Players of his caliber almost never get traded in the NBA, particularly if they haven't requested one.

Anthony Davis was still elite but injury-prone. Christie was a project. Getting those two and one first-rounder was a light return for a top-three player in the league.

The Lakers walked away with a decade-defining cornerstone. No matter how this deal ages, the optics were devastating.

This earns second place on the list of infamy because it is not about hindsight, unlike the George or Celtics-Nets deals. Everyone knew in real time how bad this was for Dallas. It is the clearest, most baffling fleece in sports history.

Anyone who disagrees likely has their checks signed by Mavs governor Patrick Dumont.

1. Paul George for Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Picks

The trade: The Clippers acquired Paul George for SGA, Danilo Gallinari, a 2021 first-round pick (via Miami), a 2022 first-round pick, a 2023 first-round pick (via Miami), a 2023 first-round pick swap, a 2024 first-round pick, a 2025 first-round pick swap and a 2026 first-round pick

At the time, Clippers fans talked themselves into this trade . It's the reason why the Clippers were able to convince Kawhi Leonard to leave the Toronto Raptors and sign with them in free agency.

However, the gamble did not pay off, to say the least. Injuries and postseason disappointments followed. Meanwhile, this deal already delivered one championship for the Thunder and has them set up for further greatness.

Not only did the Thunder get SGA, who became one of only four players in NBA history to win the regular-season MVP, Finals MVP, a scoring title and an NBA championship in the same season, but they used the Clippers' 2022 first-round pick to select Jalen Williams, who's fresh off his first All-Star appearance.

Had the damage stopped there, it would have already been one of the worst trades this century. But thanks to the salary-cap circumvention scandal involving Leonard, the damage did not stop there. The NBA stripped an additional five first-round picks from the Clippers for their role in that.

As a result, trading for George might wind up being the most costly trade in NBA history.

articles.title: After Watching World Cup, 16-Year-Old Cavan Sullivan Sets Sights On USA Call-Up
articles.summary: 16-year-old Philadelphia Union midfielder Cavan Sullivan has his sights set on the United States men's national team, as he targets a future call-up.
articles.body: 16-year-old Philadelphia Union midfielder Cavan Sullivan has his sights set on the United States men's national team, as he expressed confidence that he could make an impact in senior international matches, targeting a future call-up. Sullivan's rapid ascent up the United States soccer ladder has shaped how the teenager watches the senior national team, viewing senior team matches not just as a spectator, but as a stage he intends to reach sooner rather than later. Speaking on Alexi Lalas' State of the Union podcast, Sullivan reflected on the United States' round of 16 World Cup loss to Belgium, Sullivan expressed confidence in his ability to be an asset for the national team. "Thinking of that Belgium game, I think I could come into that game on the right side and make a difference, right? That’s just what, you have to believe in yourself, you have to think you can help your team win," Sullivan said. "It's not my team yet, but I'm obviously always dreaming and hoping call-ups." The Philadelphia Union midfielder made history at age 14, when he became not only the youngest player to appear in a Major League Soccer match, he also became the youngest player to debut in a major American or Canadian professional sports league. The hype surrounding Sullivan has mushroomed by the day in MLS and could go global by the time he is expected to transfer to Premier League powerhouse Manchester City at the end of 2027 when he is 18. Though Sullivan remains in the early stages of his career, he pays close attention to the senior national team, particularly during its recent World Cup run. Despite USA's early World Cup exit, Sullivan said he thought supporters of the team established a presence as tournament co-hosts. "The U.S. made some noise for sure, I think it was dope," Sullivan said. Sullivan pointed to Alex Freeman's header to extend USA's lead against Australia as a defining moment of the tournament. "Freeman’s header, that moment, I texted my family group chat, that actually gave me goosebumps, I think that was so cool, I think the crowd pop was insane," Sullivan said. Seeing the celebrations and hearing entire stadiums sing across the country also made a strong impression on the midfielder. "I think the country roads, all that stuff, I ate that up," Sullivan said. "I’m pretty patriotic and I love that stuff so it was really cool to see." Sullivan said he had hoped the co-hosts would make a deeper run in the tournament. "Unfortunate to lose that early, I feel like that team could have gone much farther," Sullivan added. For now, Sullivan will spend at least one more year playing stateside before potentially heading abroad to Manchester City. As the national team begins its next World Cup cycle, the 16-year-old midfielder continues working toward making the transition from watching those big tournament moments as a supporter to helping create them as a player on the international stage.

articles.title: Mike Tomlin explains why Steelers traded George Pickens
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin breaks down reasons for Steelers trading George Pickens.
articles.body:
Ahead of the 2026 NFL season, former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach and new NBC NFL analyst Mike Tomlin has been doing the media rounds, as NBC gets ready for season No. 21 of Sunday Night Football. Appearing on The Rich Eisen Show, Tomlin and the titular host discussed a variety of topics, including to the polarizing decision Pittsburgh made to trade star receiver George Pickens to the Dallas Cowboys last May.

"For us, I just thought, it's not only play. It's development in other areas, intangible areas. I think when you're a high dollar, second-contract guy, I think there's some leadership responsibilities, and things of that nature. And I just don't feel like that was in his natural wheelhouse. We felt better about DK's abilities in those areas."

Tomlin also noted that the Cowboys have been seemingly hesitant to give Pickens a second contract.

"[A second contract] didn't happen for us with George," Tomlin said. "But that doesn't necessarily mean that he's not gonna be a spectacular player. I think he's already proven that to a degree with his first year in Dallas. But there's also been something that stopped Dallas from making that long-term commitment to him, as well…"

The Steelers selected Pickens in the second round of the 2022 NFL Draft out of Georgia, where he immediately showcased the ability to make spectacular catches and big plays, but on and off-field antics were constant. From being late to meetings and games to several on-field fights and tantrums, the Steelers decided to trade away the budding star, who went on to have an All-Pro season in 2025 with the Cowboys.

articles.title: PLAYER RATINGS | Toulouse 0-1 Lille: Ayase Ueda and Berke Özer star in Lille’s smash-and-grab victory
articles.summary: Ligue 1 McDonald’s, Round 3, 03/09/2026Lille OSC came away with all three points against Toulouse FC in a game they really should have taken nothing from. Le...
articles.body:
Lille OSC came away with all three points against Toulouse FC in a game they really should have taken nothing from. Les Dogues were in debt to Berke Özer's heroics in goal and Ayase Ueda's debut off the bench. (1-0)

From the first whistle, there was a hunger about this young Toulouse side. They've yet to taste victory under summer appointment Jens Berthel Askou, and it felt like as if they had decided that they couldn't let that continue. In the third minute, Cristian Cásseres Jr. rattled the crossbar from distance to set the tempo of the half.

Ethan Mbappé was provided a huge chance a few minutes later to give Lille the lead, following a mix-up at the back from the hosts, but there was no power behind his shot. What threatened to be an end-to-end game instead became one-way traffic, as Toulouse streamed forward.

Berke Özer, often criticised and with his position somewhat less secure following the arrival of Paraguay international Orlando Gill, put in a performance to remind those of his qualities. He was in a running duel with Santiago Hidalgo and Jacen Russell-Rowe, denying them in ever more intricate ways.

Hidalgo was lucky at the start of the second half to escape without a second booking after he did a blatant dive in the box. The themes of the first half continued, with Toulouse's high press and counterpressing suffocating Lille and keeping them largely contained. However, the same goalmouth action was lacking at the start.

In the 70th minute, Guillaume Restes would have to be taken off on his 100th Ligue 1 appearance. His replacement, Mathys Niflore, would be making his debut for the club, and would soon be picking the ball out of his net as another debutant, Ayase Ueda, reacted fastest to the loose ball.

Toulouse should have answered immediately when Thomas Jørgensen fed Casper Tengstedt through on goal. Tengstedt chipped Özer, but watched as his shot carried on rising to go over the empty net. It was the story of Toulouse's night as they did everything but score.

What a performance from the Turkish international. This was a game that Lille would have lost if not for his shot-stopping abilities. Lille should be very grateful for him that they're walking away with all three points.

Replaced by Romain Perraud (5) at halftime.

Replaced by Basar Önal in the second half.

Replaced by Dilane Bakwa (5) at halftime.

A quiet one for a player who looks to be loving life under new management. There were a couple of moments that showed the player we've seen in the past two games, but they were too few and far between. Replaced by Ngal'ayel Mukau in the second half.

A game that demonstrated the limitations of the Frenchman. He offered very little when he was on the pitch, both in and out of possession. Replaced by Ayase Ueda in the second half.

The star of the first half for Toulouse. He'll be shocked that he came away from this game without having scored. His early yellow meant that he was always going to be on borrowed time, and it was clear that a change was coming when he risked a sending-off by diving at the start of the second half. Replaced in the second half by compatriot Julián Vignolo.

The attacking midfielder looks an exceptional talent. He sees space that few others do. Once it begins to click, it feels as if he's going to be a very special player.

articles.title: Durfee and New Bedford football rivalry hits Fenway Park
articles.summary: The 135th holiday meeting between Durfee and New Bedford will take place at Fenway Park this November.
articles.body:
FALL RIVER — A once in a lifetime opportunity is now offically for the Durfee football team.

The Hilltoppers and the New Bedford Whalers will renew this year's oldest high school football rivalry on the South Coast at Fenway Park — home of the Boston Red Sox.

The 135th meeting between the two schools is part of a scheduled high school doubleheader presented by Cross Insurance on Wednesday, Nov. 25, beginning at 4 p.m. "We are extremely excited and grateful to be able to play this historic football game at this historic venue," Durfee athletic director Brad Bustin said. "It will be a once in a lifetime opportunity for our players, coaches, and community."

The Hilltoppers won the last two meetings against NB, including a dominating 36-0 victory at Mac Aldrich Field on the campus of B.M.C. Durfee High School in 2025. Durfee has won three of the last five holiday meetings. The Whalers, who were winless last year, still own an overall record of 85-41-8 in the series.

Game matchups at Fenway Park are as follows:

∎ Cambridge Rindge & Latin School vs. Somerville High School – 5 p.m.

∎ Canton High School vs. Stoughton High School – 8 p.m.*

∎ Durfee High School vs. New Bedford High School – 4 p.m.

∎ Xaverian Brothers High School vs. St. John's Prep – 7 p.m.*

*Times are approximate; games are scheduled to begin 40 minutes after the conclusion of the previous contest.

General admission tickets are available for purchase at redsox.com/highschoolfootball starting at $20/ticket for each day, providing access to both games.

Twenty percent of every ticket sold will be given back to the school being supported. Dell Technologies Level Suites will be available for all matchups, starting at $50/ticket. These can be purchased by contacting Michael Gavagan at mgavagan@redsox.com .

For additional ticket information and schedule updates about this year's high school football games at Fenway Park, visit redsox.com/highschoolfootball .

"The rivalry between the Durfee Hilltoppers and the New Bedford Whalers is one of the oldest in the country," Bustin said. "There is no better place to be able to play this game than Fenway Park."

articles.title: Leandro Paredes may quit Argentina duty after suspension, Messi retirement
articles.summary: Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes has admitted his international career could be over due to his 10-game ban and the retirement of Lionel Messi.
articles.body:
Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes has admitted his international career could be over due to his 10-game ban and the retirement of longtime teammate Lionel Messi.

Messi announced his retirement from the Argentina national team on Monday, Aug. 31 , ending an international career that spanned more than two decades.

The legendary forward led Argentina to the 2026 World Cup final, where it fell 1-0 to Spain after extra time.

Paredes sparked an ugly brawl after the full-time whistle of the final, as he violently struck Spain's Eric Garcia with an open hand to the throat.

FIFA handed Paredes a 10-game suspension and $90,000 fine for his role in the melee. The midfielder's punishment was just one of many, with several other players also sanctioned.

Speaking to reporters this week, Paredes admitted that he may have played his last game for the national team.

"It's going to be difficult for me to stay with the national team," the 32-year-old said. "Because of the suspension as well, because of Leo's decision. It's going to be difficult for everything to carry on as before.

"I haven't discussed it with the coach [Lionel Scaloni] yet, but we'll talk about it and see what decision I make."

Lionel Messi’s iconic moments with Argentina national team

Paredes has been part of Argentina's setup for nearly a decade, winning the Copa America twice as well as the World Cup in 2022.

The midfielder now plays for Boca Juniors in Argentina after previously playing for Paris Saint-Germain and Roma, among other European teams.

articles.title: Hoopaholic’s Gazette: Four Questions
articles.summary: Calm down, I know it is football season. I’ll be tuned shortly. Akron at Wake Forest. Will it be the first Mac surprise of the season at ACC’s expense? Coach...
articles.body:
Calm down, I know it is football season.

I'll be tuned shortly. Akron at Wake Forest. Will it be the first Mac surprise of the season at ACC's expense? Coach Prime back in 'Lanta.

I know the Cardinals have a huge nationally televised prime time opener against an SEC power just days away in NashVegas.

I understand, even though it's 128 degrees outside it's football time.

But, you know, I am an admitted, long acknowledged hoopaholic.

Basketball is always on my mind. A junkie gotta have a fix.

Just a few things have come to mind, given some recent reminders.

The new kid in town legal gambits. Partial schedule release. An article about one of our foreigners.

U of L has been very transparent about its financial shortfall in the athletic budget. $30 mill loss built in.

So, why not offer one more money making opportunity?

Schools can now schedule three exhibition games. Louisville has two. At Kansas. In the Yum! against Division Whatever Mercyhurst, which tilt I'm sure will be included in season ticket packages.

So, why not one more moneymaker at home? Against a school of consequence that fans will want to pay to attend.

Seems like some income left on the table. A no brainer if you ask me.

Which brings me to this constructiveness query . . .

Why in this modern era does U of L not have a Basketball GM?

There are all the legal issues that have become rampant.

There's the money making imperative that's year round.

Given the basketball program's personnel, it appears that Pat Kelsey is CEO . . . and CFO . . . and Chief Recruiter . . . and Head of the Rah Rah squad . . . along with, we gotta remember . . . his coaching duties.

Anecdotal evidence tells me most legitimate programs now have a General Manager.

Kelsey has more energy and drive than your average Energizer Bunny.

But still, this is not College of Charleston.

As of now, the former Tar Heel star guard is legally able to play.

Thank you, Jefferson Circuit Judge Brian Edwards.

But that eligibility status is far from written in stone.

Fans understand what happens when a key piece of any roster goes down with a season ending injury. That's exactly what this will feel like if he projects as a starter, but 36 hours before opening game, there is a definitive ruling that he's ineligible.

The article at cnn.com a few days ago was right near the top of the home page.

Headline read, "The Chinese mavericks looking to buck the trends in American college basketball."

The opening paragraph, "C'mon Bo, C'mon Bo, C'mon Bo."

The exhortations of Cardinal hoops strength coach, Eli Foy.

The next paragraph starts, "Zhang Boyuan, a 19-year-old from northeast China . . ."

What a sec, I immediately wonder, have we been mixing up the name of this intriguing freshman since we became aware of him?

But still, a hoopaholic obsesses. About all facets of the game, no matter how much it is just minutiae.

Some quick research indicates in China, the surname comes first.

So, you understand, former pro Yao Ming's first name is Ming, not Yao.

Anyhow, I'll wrap up this much ado about zilch, with this.

Coach will surely be referring to him as Bo, not Zha. Just so you don't get confused about whom he's referring to. As if you would.

The cool thing is he's a Cardinal with a major upside, and he's the centerpiece of this article.

Alright, you can put the brats on the grille now.

articles.title: LeBron James reacts as new Rams star Myles Garrett claims No. 1 spot in NFL Top 100 rankings
articles.summary: LeBron James had the perfect response to Myles Garrett’s latest honour. The NFL’s Top 100 Players list for 2026 has Garrett at No.
articles.body:
LeBron James had the perfect response to Myles Garrett's latest honour. The NFL's Top 100 Players list for 2026 has Garrett at No. 1, and LeBron was quick to celebrate.

'YESSIR!!!!' James posted on X, reposting the NFL announcement alongside a string of fire emojis.

The two share a bond that goes back years, both coming from the Cleveland area.

Myles Garrett voted No. 1 by his peers ahead of the season

Garrett takes the top spot for the first time in his career, voted by the players themselves. Josh Allen finishes second.

It comes after a season for the ages. Garrett racked up 23 sacks in 2025, breaking the record held by T.J. Watt and Michael Strahan, while adding 60 tackles and three forced fumbles for the Browns.

The Los Angeles Rams know exactly what they have. The club responded to the news on Instagram with a simple message: 'Top of the top.'

Garrett has now been voted to seventh (2021) through the years: No. 49 in 2019, No. 80 in 2020, No. 16 in 2021, No. 11 in 2022, No. 20 in 2023, No. 5 in 2024 and No. 8 in 2025. Topped the list in 2026.

It has been a remarkable climb to the summit.

The move to Los Angeles has given him his clearest shot yet at a Super Bowl. The Rams traded for Garrett in June, sending Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second and a 2029 third to Cleveland.

He joins a defensive front that now includes the recently unretired Aaron Donald, a group that makes Los Angeles the team to beat on paper. Matthew Stafford sits No. 4 on the same list, with Puka Nacua at No. 7.

Even teammates cannot explain him. 'He's unblockable. Like there's nothing you can do,' Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain II said.

The Rams open the season with the NFL's first-ever game in Australia, facing the 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 10.

Garrett has the money, the accolades and the respect of the league. The only thing missing is a ring, and Los Angeles is built to chase exactly that.

articles.title: Manchester City star joins Benfica on loan after advice from teammate
articles.summary: Manchester City have officially confirmed that Claudio Echeverri has joined Benfica on a season-long loan deal, with the player crediting Ruben Dias and Bern...
articles.body:
Manchester City have announced that midfielder Claudio Echeverri has joined Benfica on a season-long loan. The summer transfer window in England shut at 11pm BST (5pm ET) on Tuesday. However, clubs in Portugal have until Tuesday, September 15, to complete their transactions.

This meant Echeverri's transfer to Benfica faced no immediate deadline pressure. Following his signing for the Portuguese powerhouse, the attacking midfielder revealed Ruben Dias' influence in the agreement.

"When I was in Manchester, I met with Ruben Dias. He also spoke very highly of Benfica. He told me it was a huge club, that the people here are really great, that it has a great atmosphere for playing, the atmosphere of a truly big club," Echeverri said, as per the Manchester Evening News .

"And the same was true of Bernardo Silva, who is a great player who played here. For me, he's one of the best players I've ever played with. And I listened to what he had to say, which made me even more certain that I wanted to come here. He said some wonderful things to me."

Echeverri made his City debut in the 2025 FA Cup final loss to Crystal Palace and also appeared in the season finale against Fulham. He would subsequently net his maiden goal for City in the Club World Cup victory over Al Ain in Atlanta.

Last campaign, the midfielder began the season on loan at Bayer Leverkusen but struggled to secure regular playing time. He then transferred to Girona in January.

Following his return to Manchester, he linked up with Enzo Maresca's pre-season touring party in Asia. He then remained on the bench as an unused substitute last Friday during the 4-1 triumph at Palace.

articles.title: Astros beat the White Sox 6-2 as Jose Altuve homers and Daulton Varsho triples
articles.summary: Jose Altuve hit a two-run homer and Daulton Varsho drove in two runs with a triple to lead the Houston Astros to a 6-2 victory over the Chicago White Sox on...
articles.body:
HOUSTON (AP) — Jose Altuve hit a two-run homer and Daulton Varsho drove in two runs with a triple to lead the Houston Astros to a 6-2 victory over the Chicago White Sox on Thursday.

The Astros lead the AL West by 2 1/2 games over the second-place Rangers after winning three of four games in this series against the AL Central leaders.

The game was tied and the Astros had runners on first and second with one out in the third after Luis Castillo hit Yordan Alvarez on the shoulder with a pitch.

Isaac Paredes smashed an RBI double off the left-field wall to put the Astros on top. There were two outs in the inning when Varsho's triple scored two more and push the lead to 5-2.

An RBI single by Christian Walker made it 6-2.

Castillo (4-11) yielded six hits and six runs in just four innings in the loss.

Hunter Brown (5-3) allowed six hits and two runs with seven strikeouts in six innings for his second straight win.

Miguel Vargas and Chase Meidroth had two hits each for the White Sox, who went 2 for 8 with runners in scoring position to lose for the fourth time in five games.

Paredes walked with two outs in the first before Altuve's shot to the seats in left field gave Houston an early lead.

The White Sox had runners on first and third with two outs in the second when Jake Rogers singled to cut the lead to 2-1. Sam Antonacci followed with an RBI single on a grounder to left field to tie it.

Chicago RHP Erick Fedde (7-8, 4.16 ERA) starts against RHP Zebby Matthews (9-8, 4.58) on Friday night in the opener of a three-games series against Minnesota.

articles.title: Jake Diebler hiring Jared Sullinger to Ohio State coaching staff
articles.summary: Ohio State men's basketball coach Jake Diebler is bringing former player Jared Sullinger into the fold, hiring him to his coaching staff.
articles.body:
Ohio State is bringing Jared Sullinger back into the fold.

Sullinger, a two-time All-American who starred for the Buckeyes from 2010-12, is joining coach Jake Diebler's staff in a player development role. He will replace Nick Kellogg , who was the program's NIL/community relations coordinator and is now getting out of coaching.

The move brings one of Ohio State's most accomplished players of the last 20 years back into the fold. A Northland graduate, Sullinger signed with the Buckeyes as the No. 3 national prospect in the 2010 class according to the 247Sports.com composite. He is the third-highest-rated recruit to play for Ohio State in the since the rankings began in 1999, and he quickly made a significant impact.

"Jared's love for Ohio State and his passion for helping young players grow make him a tremendous addition to our program," Diebler said in a statement. "Combine that with his basketball IQ and experience playing at the highest levels, I believe he's going to elevate our development to even greater heights. Our players will benefit from his leadership and commitment to developing the next generation of Buckeyes."

In his first season, Sullinger was named both the national and Big Ten freshman of the year and was a first-team consensus All-American as well as the most valuable player in the Big Ten Tournament while averaging 17.2 points and 10.2 rebounds as the Buckeyes went 34-3 and won the league title outright.

Before the era of name, image and likeness rights, he turned down the NBA to return for his sophomore season and was again dominant for the Buckeyes. Sullinger averaged 17.5 points and 9.2 rebounds in 2011-12 as Ohio State won a share of the Big Ten title, went 31-8 and reached the Final Four before losing a 64-62 showdown with Kansas that proved to be his final game with the Buckeyes.

He is one of only three Ohio State men's basketball players to earn multiple first-team all-America honors, joining Jim Jackson (1991-92) and Jerry Lucas (1960-62).

"Columbus is home, and Ohio State holds a special place in my heart," Sullinger said. "The tradition here, the culture, and the support from Buckeye Nation shaped me into the player and person I am today. I'm grateful to coach Diebler for the opportunity to come back and pour into these guys."

Boston picked him No. 21 overall in the 2012 NBA Draft and Sullinger played four years with the Celtics and one with Toronto, averaging 10.8 points and 7.5 rebounds while playing in 269 games across those five seasons. From there, Sullinger spent parts of the next several years playing professionally overseas while also getting involved with the Ohio State-affiliated team in The Basketball Tournament.

Sullinger coached the 2019 Carmen's Crew team to the title and then hit the winning shot to lead the team to the 2024 championship while also holding down some coaching duties . While in Columbus, Sullinger has been a consistent presence around the program, playing with alumni against the current team and generally spending time with the Buckeyes in an informal mentorship role.

His addition is the latest made by Diebler that connects this era of the program to some of its not-too-distant past. Sullinger's two seasons with the Buckeyes were played alongside William Buford, who was hired during the offseason as a program assistant. They both worked out under strength and conditioning coach Dave Richardson, who was with Ohio State from 2005-18 and rehired by Diebler during the spring.

Those three join assistant coach Dave Dickerson, who was with the Buckeyes in that role from 2010-17 and was Diebler's first hire after he was promoted to head coach at the end of the 2023-24 season.

articles.body:
Who: Ipswich Town vs Liverpool What: English Premier League Where: Portman Road, Ipswich, United Kingdom When: Friday, September 4 at 8pm (19:00 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the buildup from 16:00 GMT.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola says that Bradley Barcola arrived at the club with the “right mentality” after making clear his desire to join the Premier League club from Paris Saint-Germain.

The 24-year-old France forward became the second-most expensive signing in Liverpool’s history on Monday when he joined for a fee of up to 124 million pounds ($167m).

The price tag for the left-winger is second only to the 125 million pounds ($169m) Liverpool paid Newcastle for Sweden star Alexander Isak last year.

Iraola, who has started his Anfield tenure with two Premier League draws, welcomed the signing from the two-time defending Champions League winners, saying he would be available for Friday’s match at Ipswich.

“It was our priority, let’s say, to sign a very, very good player in that position,” the Spaniard told reporters on Thursday.

“And I think he has come also with the right mentality. I’ve learnt from him that he wanted Liverpool a lot. He just wanted to come here, and I think that’s a good first sign.

“And being the player that he is and the things that he has won recently, I think he has come also with the willingness to help us.

“And I’m very happy with him and he trained well with us. If everything goes well in today’s training, also he will definitely be available for [Ipswich].”

Iraola said a decision would be made on whether Barcola would be ready to start against newly promoted Ipswich at Portman Road.

“He is in a good place, but we also have to consider that he hasn’t had the minutes in the preseason games,” said the former Bournemouth boss.

Barcola will be part of an expensively assembled Liverpool attack that also includes Isak, Hugo Ekitike and playmaker Florian Wirtz.

The arrival of the Frenchman has raised questions about the future of left-winger Cody Gakpo, who was linked with a move away from Anfield during the summer transfer window.

But Iraola said he was happy to keep the Dutchman, whom he described as a “very valuable player”.

Iraola, who replaced the sacked Arne Slot, said he was happy with the club’s transfer business, including the signings of Barcola, Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz, and was thankful the summer window was now closed.

“The club has decided that those signings that we’ve done are the ones that improved our team, improved our position,” he said.

“There were other options that we decided not to take for different reasons. Sometimes it’s sporting reasons because they don’t improve what you have.

“Sometimes it’s because of economic reasons – it didn’t make sense in terms of the market to do those movements.

“But I’m happy now that I know what we have. I have a lot of quality in the team. Now is the moment for us, for the players, for me, to develop what we have.”

The Opta supercomputer has given Liverpool a 62 percent chance of winning the game, while giving Ipswich a 19 percent chance.

This will be the 75th meeting between the teams, with Liverpool winning 38 of the previous meetings, while Ipswich have won only 14 of the encounters.

Ipswich have problems in the centre of the pitch with Azor Matusiwa and Jack Taylor both injured, while Florentino Luis faces a late fitness test.

Jaden Philogene-Bidace also misses out with an ankle injury, while Emersonn could miss out in attack due to a knee problem.

articles.title: Bill would shift high school transfer eligibility decisions
articles.summary: (The Center Square) – The Illinois High School Association has concerns about new legislation that would allow decisions about transfer students’ athletic el...
articles.body:
(The Center Square) – The Illinois High School Association has concerns about new legislation that would allow decisions about transfer students' athletic eligibility to be made by schools.

House Bill 5808 would require the IHSA to allow high school student athletes to transfer with full eligibility if principals from both the sending and receiving schools provide written consent.

Illinois High School Association Executive Director Craig Anderson said he did not hear from state Rep. Janet Yang Rohr, D-Naperville, before she filed the bill on August 25th.

"It would be quite a difference from our current policy and residence and transfer bylaws that kind of dictate whether transfer students are eligible," Anderson told The Center Square.

Currently, the IHSA makes decisions about transfer student eligibility, but families can appeal rulings they find unfavorable.

"When the Board makes their decision and if it again is not favorable for the student, then potentially those could turn into a family deciding to file a [temporary restraining order]," Anderson said.

Anderson said Yang Rohr's bill came as a bit of a surprise, although this is the time of year when the ISHA receives a significant number of requests for transfer eligibility rulings.

"We're aware that students aren't meeting the transfer bylaw when they transfer, so we're getting some appeals to those decisions," Anderson said.

Anderson said the bill puts pressure on principals to make decisions about transfers.

"Now they're the ones who are establishing the guidance of transfer students and making those ultimate decisions, which we believe should be based upon the rules that the membership has agreed to," Anderson said.

The Illinois General Assembly could consider HB 5808 during fall veto session from Nov. 17-19 and Dec. 1-3.

When Jedd Fisch coached his first Apple Cup with the Washington Huskies in 2024, everything was different.

Fisch was three games into his first season at UW, and the former Arizona Wildcats coach had to salvage a roster with no winter transfer window and an abbreviated spring transfer period that netted multiple starting offensive linemen, a less-than-optimal lead in when facing then-fourth-year Washington State coach Jake Dickert.

The Cougars came away with a 24-19 victory over the Huskies at Lumen Field two years ago, a result that Fisch made sure wouldn't be repeated the following season when the cross-state rivals faced off last fall in Pullman.

With a school-record 59-point outing, Fisch avenged his year-one loss to Dickert; only former South Dakota State coach Jimmy Rogers was on the opposing sidelines for WSU, and this Sunday's season opener will feature a third different coach in ex-Husky graduate assistant Kirby Moore, who is now at the helm after Rogers departed for Iowa State .

"The preparation is challenging, that's for sure," Fisch said Monday during his first press conference ahead of the 118th Apple Cup this coming weekend.

"Game one. New players, new coordinators, new head coach. Really, it was kind of the opposite in our first year. They were the ones that were consistent over a few years, and we were the ones that were new. Now it becomes we're the more consistent ones, and they kind of get to know what we're doing, and we're the ones that are trying to figure it out."

Moore, a standout wide receiver under ex-UW coach Chris Petersen at Boise State from 2009-13, previously was an offensive coordinator at Missouri (2023-25) for Eli Drinkwitz, plus Kalen DeBoer and Jeff Tedford at Fresno State in various roles after his two seasons on Montlake in 2015-16.

His offensive coordinator, ex-Boise State and Montana State assistant Matt Miller, and defensive coordinator, former Oregon State head coach Trent Bray, have only faced off against Fisch once in 2023 in his last year in Tucson.

Bray, then the Beavers' defensive coordinator under Jonathan Smith, held Fisch and the Wildcats to 10 points in the first half and held star running back Jonah Coleman to his second-fewest rushing yards total—55 yards on 11 carries without a touchdown—when recording 10 or more attempts in a game in 2023.

"All together, I think there's a lot of work to be had to figure things out in the first quarter, and then go from there," Fisch added.

Given the uncertainty of what the personnel will look like on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. at Husky Stadium when UW's offense takes the field, Fisch knows it's going to be a unique challenge to open the 2026 season.
